contraindications: Inability to maintain a stable setup
exercise_setup: Place a flat bench under the rack, align the eyes slightly behind the bar, plant both feet, and grip the bar evenly.
execution_steps: Unrack with elbows extended
Lower the bar under control toward the lower-to-mid chest
Press upward while maintaining upper-back tension
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace before lowering; exhale after passing the sticking region.

exercise_setup: Sit on the bench with the dumbbells on the thighs, lie back under control, and position the dumbbells beside the chest.
execution_steps: Press the dumbbells upward
Lower them under control through a comfortable range
Maintain forearm alignment under the dumbbells
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering; exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Adjust the seat so the handles align near mid-chest and keep the back supported.
execution_steps: Grip the handles
Press forward without forcefully locking the elbows
Return under control to a comfortable stretch
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pressing; inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Place the hands slightly wider than shoulder width and create a straight line from head to heels.
execution_steps: Lower the chest between the hands
Keep the elbows at a comfortable angle
Press the floor away to return
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering; exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Set the bench to a moderate incline and position the dumbbells beside the upper chest.
execution_steps: Press upward and slightly inward
Lower under control until a comfortable upper-chest stretch
Maintain even arm paths
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering; exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Sit with the feet supported, knees slightly bent, torso tall, and hold the handle.
execution_steps: Initiate by drawing the shoulder blades back
Pull the handle toward the lower ribs
Return under control without collapsing the torso
breathing_pattern: Exhale while rowing; inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Set an incline bench, lie chest-down, and let the dumbbells hang beneath the shoulders.
execution_steps: Pull the elbows toward the hips or ribs
Pause briefly without shrugging
Lower the dumbbells under control
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest off the bench
breathing_pattern: Exhale while rowing; inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Support one hand and knee on a bench, keep the spine neutral, and hold the dumbbell in the free hand.
execution_steps: Pull the dumbbell toward the hip
Keep the trunk mostly still
Lower until the shoulder blade can move forward under control
cues: Drive the elbow toward the hip
breathing_pattern: Exhale while rowing; inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Adjust the seat and chest support so the handles can be reached without rounding the torso.
execution_steps: Pull the handles toward the ribs
Keep the chest supported
Return under control to a comfortable stretch
cues: Keep the chest on the pad
breathing_pattern: Exhale while rowing; inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Set a secure bar at a suitable height, grip it, and position the body in a straight line.
execution_steps: Pull the chest toward the bar
Keep the hips extended
Lower under control until the arms are straight
common_mistakes: Pulling the chin instead of the chest
cues: Pull the chest to the bar
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling; inhale while lowering.

contraindications: Inability to control the hanging position
exercise_setup: Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with a pronated grip, hang with the ribs controlled, and set the shoulders away from the ears.
execution_steps: Initiate by depressing the scapulae
Pull the elbows down and toward the ribs
Raise the chest toward the bar without excessive swinging
Lower under control to a comfortable full hang
common_mistakes: Stopping far short of the top
breathing_pattern: Inhale in the bottom position; exhale while pulling and re-brace before descending.

exercise_setup: Use a shoulder-width supinated grip, begin from a controlled hang, and keep the trunk rigid.
execution_steps: Depress the shoulder blades
Pull the elbows down and back
Bring the upper chest toward the bar
Lower smoothly without losing shoulder control
breathing_pattern: Inhale before the pull; exhale through the concentric phase and reset at the bottom.

contraindications: Inability to maintain an upright torso
exercise_setup: Sit with the thighs secured, grip the bar wider than shoulder width, and lean back only slightly.
execution_steps: Depress the scapulae before bending the elbows
Pull the bar toward the upper chest
Keep the forearms roughly aligned with the cable
Return under control to full overhead reach
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling down; inhale during the controlled return.

exercise_setup: Secure the thighs, use a neutral grip, sit upright, and begin with the arms overhead.
execution_steps: Set the shoulder blades down
Drive the elbows toward the floor
Pull the handle toward the upper chest
Return slowly until the lats are lengthened
common_mistakes: Turning the movement into a row
breathing_pattern: Exhale during the pull; inhale during the return.

contraindications: Inability to maintain a hip hinge
exercise_setup: Stand over the bar, hinge at the hips, brace the trunk, and hold the bar with the arms hanging below the shoulders.
execution_steps: Maintain a fixed torso angle
Pull the bar toward the lower ribs or upper abdomen
Retract the shoulder blades without jerking
Lower the bar under control
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace before pulling; exhale after the bar passes the hardest point.

exercise_setup: Straddle the bar or enter the machine, hinge at the hips, brace, and allow the arms to hang toward the loading point.
execution_steps: Pull the handle toward the lower chest or upper abdomen
Keep the torso stable
Squeeze the shoulder blades together
Return until the back muscles are lengthened
breathing_pattern: Brace before pulling; exhale near the top and inhale during the return.

exercise_setup: Sit or stand square to the cable, hold one handle, brace the trunk, and reach forward without collapsing the spine.
execution_steps: Initiate with controlled scapular movement
Pull the elbow toward the hip or ribs
Resist torso rotation
Return until the shoulder blade protracts comfortably
breathing_pattern: Exhale while rowing; inhale during the return.

exercise_setup: Stand facing a high cable, hold the attachment with nearly straight elbows, hinge slightly, and brace the ribs down.
execution_steps: Sweep the arms down toward the thighs
Keep elbow angle nearly constant
Avoid leaning back
Return slowly into an overhead stretch
common_mistakes: Turning the exercise into a triceps pushdown
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling down; inhale during the overhead return.

exercise_setup: Set the cable near face height, hold the rope with neutral grips, step back, and brace the torso.
execution_steps: Pull the rope toward the forehead or nose
Separate the handles
Externally rotate so the hands finish beside the face
Return under control
cues: Pause with hands beside the face
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling; inhale during the return.

exercise_setup: Lie across or along a flat bench, hold one dumbbell securely above the chest, keep a slight elbow bend, and brace the trunk.
execution_steps: Lower the dumbbell behind the head through a comfortable range of motion
Maintain a nearly fixed elbow angle
Keep the ribs controlled
Pull the dumbbell back above the chest
common_mistakes: Turning the exercise into a skull crusher
breathing_pattern: Inhale during the lowering phase; exhale while returning the dumbbell.

exercise_setup: Adjust the seat back and shin pad so your knee aligns with the machine's axis of rotation.
execution_steps: Grip the handles firmly.
Extend your knees to push the pad upward until your legs are fully straight.
Squeeze the quads hard at the top.
Lower the weight slowly under control.
common_mistakes: Using momentum to swing the weight up
Lifting the glutes off the seat
breathing_pattern: Exhale while extending the legs, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit on a bench with back support, holding dumbbells at shoulder height with palms facing forward.
execution_steps: Brace your core and press the dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower the dumbbells under control back to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Not locking out at the top
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pressing up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand next to a low cable pulley, grab the handle with the outside hand, and take a slight lean away from the machine.
execution_steps: Keeping a slight bend in the elbow, raise the arm out to the side until it reaches shoulder height.
Pause for a second at the top.
Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position.
breathing_pattern: Exhale while raising the arm, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Adjust the seat so the handles are roughly level with your shoulders. Sit back completely against the pad.
execution_steps: Grip the handles and press upward until the arms are extended.
Do not lock out the elbows forcefully.
Lower the weight slowly to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Allowing elbows to flare too far back
Lifting the lower back off the pad
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pressing, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Adjust the seat so the handles are at shoulder level. Sit facing the machine pad with your chest supported.
execution_steps: Grip the handles and push your arms out and back in an arc.
Squeeze your rear delts and upper back at the end of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position.
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling back, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Lie face down, then prop yourself up on your forearms and toes. Elbows should be directly under the shoulders.
execution_steps: Engage your core, glutes, and quads to maintain a perfectly straight line from head to heels.
Hold this position while breathing deeply and steadily.
Do not allow the hips to sag or pike up.
common_mistakes: Looking up and straining the neck
cues: Brace like you are about to be punched in the stomach
Push the floor away with your elbows
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously and rhythmically; do not hold your breath.

exercise_setup: Attach a rope to a high cable pulley. Kneel facing the machine and hold the rope ends beside your ears.
execution_steps: Flex your spine to crunch your torso downward, bringing your elbows toward your knees.
Squeeze the abs hard at the bottom.
Slowly return to the starting position without extending the lower back excessively.
common_mistakes: Using the arms to pull the weight
Flexing at the hips instead of the spine
cues: Crunch the ribs to the pelvis
breathing_pattern: Exhale forcefully while crunching down, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, legs straight down.
execution_steps: Engage your core and pull your legs up toward the bar by flexing the hips and spine.
Squeeze the abs at the top of the movement.
Lower the legs back down under strict control to avoid swinging.
common_mistakes: Using momentum to swing the legs
Only flexing the hips without rounding the pelvis
cues: Don't just lift the legs, crunch the abs
breathing_pattern: Exhale while lifting the legs, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Kneel on a mat with your hands on the ab wheel directly under your shoulders.
execution_steps: Brace your core and slowly roll the wheel forward as far as you can without letting your lower back sag.
Pause briefly at maximum extension.
Use your core and lats to pull the wheel back to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Hinging back at the hips too early
cues: Don't let the lower back break
breathing_pattern: Inhale before rolling out, exhale while pulling back.

exercise_setup: Stand perpendicular to a cable pulley holding the handle with both hands at your chest.
execution_steps: Brace your core and press the handle straight out in front of you.
Resist the urge to let the cable rotate your torso.
Hold for a few seconds, then return the handle to your chest.
cues: Press in a perfectly straight line
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pressing out, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Stand holding a barbell with an overhand grip slightly narrower than shoulder-width.
execution_steps: Pull the barbell straight up close to your body until it reaches your upper chest.
Lead with the elbows, keeping them higher than the wrists.
Lower the bar back to the starting position under control.
cues: Keep the bar close to the shirt
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand tall holding a barbell with a supinated (underhand) grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
execution_steps: Keeping elbows pinned to your sides, curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze the biceps hard at the top.
Lower the bar back to the starting position under control.
common_mistakes: Using momentum to swing the weight
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand facing a high cable pulley with a rope or straight bar attachment. Brace your core and hinge slightly forward.
execution_steps: Pin your elbows to your sides and push the attachment down until your arms are fully extended.
Squeeze the triceps at the bottom.
Return slowly to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Letting elbows flare out or move forward
Using body weight to push down
cues: Spread the rope at the bottom
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pushing down, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Step onto the calf block with the balls of your feet, placing your shoulders under the pads. Unrack the weight.
execution_steps: Lower your heels as far as comfortable to stretch the calves.
Press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
Pause and squeeze at the top.
common_mistakes: Not going through a full range of motion
breathing_pattern: Exhale while raising heels, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit on the machine, place the balls of your feet on the platform, and secure the knee pads over your lower thighs.
execution_steps: Release the safety lever and lower your heels to feel a stretch.
Drive through the balls of your feet to lift the heels as high as possible.
Slowly lower back down.
common_mistakes: Using toes instead of the ball of the foot
breathing_pattern: Exhale while lifting, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Lie flat on a bench holding an EZ-bar with a narrow overhand grip, arms extended straight up.
execution_steps: Keeping your upper arms stationary, bend your elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead or just behind your head.
Feel the stretch in the triceps, then extend your elbows to return to the top.
Maintain control and proper breathing throughout the entire movement.
common_mistakes: Moving the upper arms too much
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering the bar, exhale while pressing back up.

exercise_setup: Stand holding a pair of dumbbells by your sides with a neutral grip (palms facing your body).
execution_steps: Keeping your elbows pinned to your sides, curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders.
Maintain the neutral grip throughout the entire movement.
Lower the weights under control.
common_mistakes: Turning the wrist into a supinated curl
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench. Roll a padded barbell over your hips and plant your feet firmly.
execution_steps: Drive through your heels to extend your hips upward until your thighs and torso are parallel to the floor.
Squeeze the glutes hard at the top.
Lower the hips back down under control.
cues: Squeeze the glutes, not the back
breathing_pattern: Inhale before driving up, exhale at the top.

exercise_setup: Rest the barbell on the front of your shoulders, pointing your elbows forward to secure the bar. Step back from the rack.
execution_steps: Keeping your torso highly upright, descend by bending the hips and knees.
Squat until your hips are below your knees.
Drive back up to the starting position.
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace before descending, exhale on the way up.

exercise_setup: Stand holding a pair of dumbbells by your sides. Brace your core.
execution_steps: Step forward with one leg and lower your hips until both knees are bent at a 90-degree angle.
Drive through the heel of the front foot to step forward into the next lunge with the opposite leg.
Maintain control and proper breathing throughout the entire movement.
common_mistakes: Taking steps that are too short or too long
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pushing up.

exercise_setup: Set a barbell on your upper back as if you were doing a back squat. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
execution_steps: Keeping a slight bend in the knees and a perfectly flat back, hinge at the hips to push your glutes backward.
Lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glutes and hamstrings to stand back up.
common_mistakes: Bending the knees too much into a squat
cues: Feel the stretch in the hamstrings
breathing_pattern: Inhale while hinging forward, exhale while returning to the start.

exercise_setup: Stand holding a pair of dumbbells in front of your thighs with a pronated grip. Keep your feet shoulder-width apart.
execution_steps: Maintain a slight bend in your knees and a rigid, straight back.
Push your hips back as far as possible, lowering the dumbbells along your legs until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to return to the standing position, squeezing your glutes at the top.
common_mistakes: Bending the knees too much (turning it into a squat)
Letting the dumbbells drift away from the body
cues: Shave your legs with the dumbbells
Push your hips to the wall behind you
breathing_pattern: Inhale while hinging forward, exhale while standing up.

exercise_setup: Lie face down on the machine pad, ensuring your knees align with the pivot point. Hook your heels under the roller pad.
execution_steps: Flex your knees to curl the pad toward your glutes.
Squeeze your hamstrings hard at the peak of the contraction.
Lower the pad back to the starting position under slow control.
common_mistakes: Lifting the hips off the pad to cheat
Using momentum to swing the weight
cues: Press your hips firmly into the pad
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling the weight, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit in the machine with your back flat against the pad. Adjust the thigh pad so it rests securely just above your knees, and hook your ankles over the roller.
execution_steps: Pull the pad downward and back by flexing your knees as far as comfortably possible.
Pause and squeeze the hamstrings at the bottom.
Return slowly to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Setting the thigh pad too loose
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling down, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Attach a rope to a low cable pulley. Stand facing away from the machine, straddling the cable, and hold the rope ends between your legs.
execution_steps: Walk forward a few steps to create tension. Keep a soft bend in your knees.
Hinge at the hips, pushing them back toward the machine while letting your hands go through your legs.
Drive your hips forward to stand up straight, squeezing your glutes intensely.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms instead of driving with the hips
Hyperextending the lower back at the top
cues: Push hips to the cable tower
breathing_pattern: Inhale while hinging back, exhale while driving forward.

exercise_setup: Lie on your back on a mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
execution_steps: Brace your core and drive through your heels to lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes tightly at the top.
Lower your hips back to the floor under control.
common_mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back instead of using the glutes
Pushing through the toes instead of the heels
cues: Squeeze glutes hard at the top
breathing_pattern: Exhale while lifting the hips, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit in the machine and place your outer thighs against the pads. Set the starting width so you feel a mild stretch.
execution_steps: Press your legs outward against the pads as far as you can.
Pause and squeeze your outer glutes at the widest point.
Slowly return to the starting position without letting the weight stack crash.
common_mistakes: Using momentum to slam the pads open
Leaning too far forward or back to cheat
cues: Squeeze the side of the glutes
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pushing out, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Sit in the machine and place your inner thighs against the pads. Adjust the starting position out wide so you feel a stretch in the groin.
execution_steps: Squeeze your thighs together to bring the pads toward the midline of your body.
Pause when the pads touch.
Slowly open your legs back to the starting stretched position.
common_mistakes: Setting the stretch too wide causing pain
breathing_pattern: Exhale while bringing legs together, inhale while opening.

exercise_setup: Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, the kettlebell on the floor slightly in front of you. Hinge down and grip the handle with both hands.
execution_steps: Hike the kettlebell back between your legs like a football.
Explosively drive your hips forward to swing the kettlebell up to chest height.
Let the kettlebell swing back down between your legs naturally, hinging at the hips as it passes through.
common_mistakes: Using the arms to lift the bell (front raise)
Hyperextending the back at the top
cues: Arms act as ropes, not motors
breathing_pattern: Inhale as the bell swings down, exhale sharply as the hips snap forward.

contraindications: History of severe hamstring tears without clearance
exercise_setup: Kneel on a soft pad while a partner holds your ankles securely to the floor (or use a secure anchor). Keep your torso tall and hips fully extended.
execution_steps: Slowly lower your torso forward toward the floor, using your hamstrings to resist gravity.
Go as far as you can control, then use your hands to catch yourself on the floor.
Push off slightly with your hands and use your hamstrings to pull yourself back to the starting upright position.
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips instead of keeping a straight line
Dropping too fast without trying to resist
Not using hands to catch the fall
cues: Fight the fall as long as possible
breathing_pattern: Inhale deeply before starting the descent, exhale on the push up.

exercise_setup: Adjust the machine so the hip pad rests just below your pelvis, allowing free hip flexion. Secure your feet under the ankle pads.
execution_steps: Cross your arms over your chest or hold a weight plate. Hinge forward at the hips, lowering your torso as far as comfortable.
Engage your glutes, hamstrings, and lower back to raise your torso until your body forms a straight line.
Pause and squeeze at the top.
common_mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back at the top
Rounding the spine excessively instead of hinging at the hips
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while raising the torso.

exercise_setup: Position your back flat against the backrest and shoulders under the shoulder pads. Place your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform.
execution_steps: Lower the carriage by bending your knees and hips until your thighs are at least parallel to the platform.
Drive through your entire foot to push the carriage back to the starting position.
Maintain control and proper breathing throughout the entire movement.
common_mistakes: Lifting the heels off the platform
cues: Keep lower back pressed into the pad
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering the weight, exhale while pushing up.

exercise_setup: Set the pulleys to a high position. Grab a handle in each hand, step forward to create tension, and adopt a staggered stance.
execution_steps: With a slight bend in your elbows, pull the handles down and across your body in a hugging motion.
Squeeze your chest at the bottom of the movement.
Slowly let the handles return to the starting position, feeling a stretch in the chest.
common_mistakes: Pressing the weight instead of flying
cues: Keep elbows slightly bent and locked in that position
Squeeze the chest at the bottom
breathing_pattern: Exhale while bringing the handles together, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Adjust the seat height so the handles are at chest level. Sit flat against the backrest.
execution_steps: Grip the handles and push your arms together in front of your chest.
Squeeze your pectoral muscles hard when the handles meet.
Slowly allow your arms to return to the starting position until you feel a comfortable stretch.
common_mistakes: Over-stretching the shoulders on the return
breathing_pattern: Exhale while bringing arms together, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Set an adjustable bench to a 30-45 degree incline. Lie back holding dumbbells directly above your chest with a neutral grip.
execution_steps: With a slight bend in your elbows, slowly lower the dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc.
Stop when you feel a stretch in your chest (dumbbells roughly level with your chest).
Squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Turning the movement into an incline press
Lowering the weight too far and stressing the shoulder capsule
cues: Maintain a soft bend in the elbows
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering the dumbbells, exhale while bringing them together.

exercise_setup: Sit at a preacher bench and adjust the seat height so your armpits rest comfortably on the top of the pad. Grab an EZ-bar with an underhand grip.
execution_steps: Lower the bar slowly until your arms are fully extended, feeling a stretch in the biceps.
Curl the bar upward, squeezing the biceps at the top of the movement.
Do not let the tension off the biceps at the top.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to cheat the weight up
Hyperextending the elbows at the bottom
Not using a full range of motion
cues: Keep the back of your arms glued to the pad
Control the descent to protect the tendon
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering the bar, exhale while curling.

exercise_setup: Sit on the edge of a bench with your legs spread. Rest the back of your working arm's triceps against your inner thigh.
execution_steps: Curl the dumbbell upward toward your chest, isolating the biceps.
Squeeze the muscle hard at the peak contraction.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Using the thigh to bounce the arm up
cues: Keep the upper arm perfectly still
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit on a bench with back support. Hold one heavy dumbbell with both hands (palms under the inner plate) and press it overhead.
execution_steps: Keeping your elbows pointing up and upper arms stationary, lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Feel a deep stretch in the triceps.
Extend your elbows to press the dumbbell back to the starting overhead position.
common_mistakes: Flaring the elbows out too wide
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering the weight, exhale while extending.

exercise_setup: Stand tall holding a pair of heavy dumbbells by your sides with a neutral grip.
execution_steps: Keeping your arms perfectly straight, elevate your shoulders as high as possible toward your ears.
Hold the contraction for a second at the top.
Lower your shoulders back to a full dead hang stretch.
common_mistakes: Rolling the shoulders forward or backward
Bending the elbows to cheat the weight up
cues: Shrug straight up to your ears
Hold the squeeze at the top
breathing_pattern: Exhale while shrugging up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit on a bench and rest your forearms on your thighs or the bench pad. Hold a barbell with an underhand (supinated) grip, allowing your wrists to hang off the edge.
execution_steps: Let the barbell roll down to the tips of your fingers to fully stretch the forearms.
Curl the barbell back up by closing your hands and flexing your wrists as high as possible.
Squeeze the forearm muscles at the top.
common_mistakes: Lifting the forearms off the bench
Using excessive weight and shortening the ROM
cues: Let the bar roll to the fingertips
Keep forearms glued to the bench
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while curling the wrists.

exercise_setup: Sit on a bench and rest your forearms on your thighs or the bench pad. Hold a barbell with an overhand (pronated) grip, wrists hanging off the edge.
execution_steps: Lower the barbell by letting your wrists drop as far as comfortable.
Extend your wrists upward to lift the barbell as high as possible.
Squeeze the extensor muscles at the top.
common_mistakes: Moving the forearms off the pad
Using the biceps to lift the weight
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while extending the wrists.

exercise_setup: Sit in the leg press machine and place only the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform.
execution_steps: Keeping your knees straight but not forcefully locked, lower the toes toward you to stretch the calves.
Press through the balls of your feet to push the platform up as far as possible.
Squeeze the calves hard at the top.
common_mistakes: Bending the knees during the movement
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pressing up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Set an adjustable bench to a 45-60 degree incline. Sit back holding a dumbbell in each hand, letting your arms hang straight down to feel a stretch in the biceps.
execution_steps: Keeping your upper arms completely still and pointing at the floor, curl the weights up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze the biceps at the top.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to the full hang.
common_mistakes: Not letting the arms hang fully at the bottom
Lifting the head off the bench
cues: Feel the stretch at the bottom
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Set a cable pulley to the highest position. Stand sideways to the machine, holding the handle with both hands.
execution_steps: Keep your arms relatively straight and pull the handle diagonally down across your body toward your opposite knee.
Allow your torso to rotate with the movement, pivoting your back foot slightly.
Return slowly to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Using only the arms instead of rotating the torso
breathing_pattern: Exhale while chopping down, inhale while returning.

contraindications: Glaucoma or high blood pressure (due to decline angle)
exercise_setup: Secure your feet under the pads of a decline bench. Unrack the barbell with a grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
execution_steps: Lower the bar in a controlled manner to your lower chest.
Pause briefly without bouncing the bar off your chest.
Press the bar powerfully back up to lockout.
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Stand on a 1-3 inch elevated platform or weight plate. The barbell remains on the floor, increasing the range of motion.
execution_steps: Hinge down to grip the bar, keeping your chest up and back flat.
Drive through the floor, extending your hips and knees to stand up completely.
Lower the bar back to the floor under control.
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back due to lack of mobility
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace before the pull, exhale at the lockout.

exercise_setup: Stand holding a barbell with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, letting it hang in front of your thighs.
execution_steps: Keep your arms straight and shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Hold the contraction for a second.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position to stretch the traps.
breathing_pattern: Exhale while shrugging, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Hold a pair of light dumbbells, hinge at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, let arms hang with a slight elbow bend.
execution_steps: Raise the dumbbells out to the sides in an arc until they are parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your rear delts and upper back.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Using momentum to swing the weight
Retracting the scapula too much instead of isolating rear delts
breathing_pattern: Exhale while raising the weights, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Lie on a flat bench and grip the barbell with hands roughly shoulder-width apart (closer than a standard bench press).
execution_steps: Unrack the bar and lower it to your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked close to your torso.
Pause briefly.
Press the bar back up to full elbow lockout, squeezing the triceps.
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Set the bar at upper-chest height. Step under it, rest it on your upper back, and place your feet slightly forward.
execution_steps: Unrack the bar, lower your hips by bending your knees until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Drive through your heels to return to a standing position.
Maintain control and proper breathing throughout the entire movement.
common_mistakes: Placing feet too far directly under the bar (stresses knees awkwardly)
breathing_pattern: Inhale while descending, exhale while ascending.

exercise_setup: Adjust the seat so the handles align with your upper chest. Sit with your back firmly against the pad.
execution_steps: Grip the handles and press forward and upward until your arms are extended.
Return the handles slowly to the starting position, feeling a stretch in the upper chest.
Maintain control and proper breathing throughout the entire movement.
common_mistakes: Lifting the lower back off the pad
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pressing, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Stand in front of a box or bench holding dumbbells by your sides.
execution_steps: Place one foot entirely on the box.
Drive through the heel of the elevated foot to step up until the leg is straight.
Slowly lower your trailing leg back to the floor under control.
common_mistakes: Pushing off too much with the back leg
Letting the front knee cave inward
breathing_pattern: Exhale while stepping up, inhale while stepping down.

exercise_setup: Stand between two heavy dumbbells or kettlebells. Hinge down with a flat back and grip them firmly.
execution_steps: Stand up completely straight, bracing your core and pulling your shoulder blades back and down.
Walk forward with short, quick, and stable steps.
Maintain an upright posture throughout the walk.
common_mistakes: Leaning forward or to the side
Taking steps that are too long
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously and shallowly into the braced core.

exercise_setup: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet lifted slightly off the ground. Lean back to a 45-degree angle, holding a weight in front of your chest.
execution_steps: Twist your torso to the right, bringing the weight toward the floor beside your hip.
Twist your torso back to the center and then to the left side.
Keep your legs as still as possible.
common_mistakes: Only moving the arms and not rotating the torso
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously, exhaling at the end of each twist.
regressions: Feet on the floor Russian Twist

exercise_setup: Stand next to a sturdy object for balance. Rise up onto your toes.
execution_steps: Keeping your hips fully extended (body in a straight line from knees to shoulders), lean backward.
Bend your knees to lower your body toward the floor, driving your knees forward.
Use your quads to pull yourself back to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips (turning it into a regular squat)
cues: Straight line from knee to shoulder
breathing_pattern: Inhale on the way down, exhale on the way up.

exercise_setup: Sit on a bench with a backrest holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms fully extended by your sides.
execution_steps: Keeping your upper arms stationary, curl the weights up while rotating your palms to face your shoulders (supination).
Squeeze the biceps at the top.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position under control.
common_mistakes: Using momentum by swinging the torso
Not fully extending the arms at the bottom
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand facing a low cable pulley holding a straight bar attachment with an underhand grip.
execution_steps: Keep your elbows tucked to your sides.
Curl the bar up toward your chest, squeezing the biceps hard at the peak.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position, maintaining constant tension.
common_mistakes: Letting elbows drift forward (turning it into a front raise)
Using excessive weight and leaning back
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Mount the parallel bars, locking your elbows and keeping your torso relatively upright to target the triceps.
execution_steps: Lower your body by bending your elbows until they reach a 90-degree angle.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your body.
Press forcefully back up to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Flaring elbows out too much (shifts focus to chest and strains shoulders)
Going too deep and over-stretching the shoulder capsule
Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing up.

exercise_setup: Position yourself in the machine with the pad resting across your lower back/pelvis. Place the balls of your feet on the edge of the step.
execution_steps: Lower your heels as far as possible to deeply stretch the calves.
Push through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
Hold the contraction for a second at the top.
common_mistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom position
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pushing up.

exercise_setup: Stand holding a pair of dumbbells in front of your thighs with a pronated (overhand) grip.
execution_steps: Keeping your arms straight with a slight micro-bend in the elbows, raise the dumbbells straight out in front of you to shoulder level.
Pause briefly.
Lower the weights slowly back to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Using momentum by swinging the torso backward
Raising the weights too high (above eye level)
breathing_pattern: Exhale while raising, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit on a bench with back support. Hold two dumbbells in front of your face with a supinated grip (palms facing you).
execution_steps: Press the dumbbells overhead while simultaneously rotating your wrists outwards.
Finish with the arms fully extended and palms facing forward (pronated grip).
Reverse the motion to lower the dumbbells back in front of your face.
common_mistakes: Using weights that are too heavy for the rotational component
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pressing up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand perpendicular to a landmine barbell. Hinge at the hips, stagger your stance, and grip the thick end of the bar with an overhand grip.
execution_steps: Row the barbell up toward your hip/ribcage, letting your elbow flare out slightly to target the upper back and lats.
Squeeze your back muscles at the top.
Lower the bar under control until your scapula stretches forward.
common_mistakes: Using too much torso rotation to swing the weight
Not letting the shoulder blade stretch at the bottom
breathing_pattern: Exhale while rowing, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Set the barbell in a rack slightly below elbow height. Cradle the bar in the crooks of your elbows, holding your hands together.
execution_steps: Step back from the rack, keep your chest extremely upright, and brace your core.
Squat down by bending your knees and hips until your elbows touch or go between your thighs.
Drive through your feet to stand back up.
common_mistakes: Letting the bar roll down the forearms
cues: Squeeze the bar into your body
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace before descending, exhale on the way up.

exercise_setup: Stand on one leg with the other leg extended straight out in front of you. Extend your arms forward for balance.
execution_steps: Lower your body by bending the knee and hip of your standing leg.
Descend until your hamstring rests on your calf.
Drive through your foot to push yourself back up to a standing position without letting the raised foot touch the floor.
common_mistakes: Heel of the standing foot lifting off the floor
Rounding the lower back excessively at the bottom
breathing_pattern: Inhale while descending, exhale while pushing up.

exercise_setup: Sit in the machine and secure your feet or legs behind the pads. Grab the upper handles.
execution_steps: Using your abdominal muscles, crunch your torso forward, bringing your ribs toward your pelvis.
Squeeze the abs hard at the point of maximum contraction.
Slowly return to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms instead of the abs
Arching the lower back on the return
breathing_pattern: Exhale while crunching, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Sit or stand at the shrug machine and grab the handles with a neutral grip.
execution_steps: Keep your arms straight and elevate your shoulders toward your ears.
Squeeze the traps at the top of the movement.
Lower the handles back down to a full stretch.
breathing_pattern: Exhale while shrugging, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Face the backrest of the hack squat machine. Position your shoulders under the pads and feet on the platform.
execution_steps: Lower the carriage by bending your hips and knees, pushing your hips back as if doing a traditional squat.
Squat until your thighs are parallel to the platform.
Drive through your feet to push the carriage back up.
breathing_pattern: Inhale while descending, exhale while ascending.

exercise_setup: Position yourself on the GHR machine with your feet secured and knees resting just behind the hip pad.
execution_steps: Start with your torso upright. Lower your body under control until you are parallel to the floor.
Use your hamstrings and glutes to pull your body back up to the vertical starting position.
Maintain a straight line from knees to shoulders.
common_mistakes: Breaking at the hips instead of the knees
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pulling up.

exercise_setup: Grab the TRX handles and lean back until your arms are straight. Walk your feet forward to increase the angle and difficulty. Keep your body in a straight line.
execution_steps: Retract your shoulder blades and pull your chest up to the handles.
Pause and squeeze your upper back.
Slowly lower your body back to the starting position.
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand with a staggered stance holding the end of a landmine barbell at shoulder height with one hand.
execution_steps: Brace your core and press the barbell up and forward until your arm is fully extended.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower the barbell under control back to your shoulder.
common_mistakes: Using leg drive (turning it into a push press)
Letting the elbow flare out too much
cues: Follow the path of the bar
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pressing, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Take a very wide stance with your toes pointed outward. Grip the bar inside your knees.
execution_steps: Drop your hips, lift your chest, and pull the slack out of the bar.
Drive through the floor with your legs, keeping your torso as upright as possible.
Lock out your hips and knees simultaneously at the top.
cues: Spread the floor with your feet
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace hard before the pull, exhale at lockout.

exercise_setup: Step inside the trap bar. Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the handles securely.
execution_steps: Lower your hips and lift your chest.
Drive through your feet to stand up straight, extending hips and knees.
Return the weight to the floor under control.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a stiff-legged deadlift
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace before lifting, exhale at the top.

exercise_setup: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell vertically against your chest with both hands. Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width.
execution_steps: Keeping your chest up and core braced, sit your hips back and down.
Squat until your elbows touch the inside of your knees.
Drive through your entire foot to stand back up.
common_mistakes: Letting the weight pull you forward
cues: Keep the weight glued to your chest
breathing_pattern: Inhale while descending, exhale while standing up.

exercise_setup: Set a box behind you to your desired squat depth. Unrack the barbell on your upper back and take a slightly wider stance.
execution_steps: Push your hips far back and sit back onto the box completely, pausing for a split second.
Do not rock backward; maintain core tension.
Explosively drive through the floor to stand back up.
common_mistakes: Losing core tension on the box
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace before descending, exhale upon exploding up.

exercise_setup: Hold the barbell in a front rack position, resting on your shoulders. Feet shoulder-width apart.
execution_steps: Perform a shallow dip by bending your knees slightly while keeping your torso perfectly upright.
Explosively drive your legs to launch the bar upward.
Finish pressing the bar overhead with your arms until elbows lock out.
common_mistakes: Dipping too low (turning it into a squat)
Pressing early before the leg drive is finished
cues: Head through the window at the top
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace before the dip, exhale at lockout.

exercise_setup: Lie on your back on the floor inside a power rack with your knees bent. Unrack the barbell like a bench press.
execution_steps: Lower the barbell slowly until your triceps (back of the upper arms) rest completely on the floor.
Pause for a second, letting the floor absorb the momentum.
Press the bar explosively back to lockout.
common_mistakes: Bouncing the elbows off the floor
Lifting the hips to cheat the weight up
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Set up exactly like a standard barbell bench press. Unrack the weight.
execution_steps: Lower the bar under extreme control until it is about 1-2 inches hovering above your chest.
Pause motionless in the air for 1-2 seconds, maintaining maximum tension in the chest and lats.
Explode back to the top.
common_mistakes: Sinking the bar during the pause
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace while lowering, hold breath during pause, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Lie face down on the machine's chest pad. Plant your feet firmly on the footplates and grab the handles.
execution_steps: Pull the handles upward by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause at the top of the movement.
Lower the weight slowly until your arms are fully extended and shoulder blades stretched.
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad to cheat
Pulling with the biceps instead of the back
cues: Keep chest glued to the pad
breathing_pattern: Exhale while rowing, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Get into a high plank position holding a dumbbell in each hand directly under your shoulders. Spread your feet wide for balance.
execution_steps: Brace your core to prevent your hips from twisting.
Row one dumbbell up to your ribcage while balancing on the other arm and your feet.
Lower the dumbbell under control, and repeat on the other side.
common_mistakes: Twisting the hips/torso to lift the weight
cues: Push the floor away with the non-working arm
breathing_pattern: Exhale while rowing, inhale while returning.
progressions: Feet closer together for more core instability

exercise_setup: Stand holding a pair of dumbbells by your sides.
execution_steps: Curl the dumbbells up using a supinated (underhand) grip.
At the top of the curl, rotate your hands so your palms face downward (pronated grip).
Lower the dumbbells under control using this overhand grip. Rotate back to underhand at the bottom.
common_mistakes: Rushing the rotation at the top
cues: Control the negative for forearm growth
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Lie face down on a 45-degree incline bench with your arms hanging straight down, holding dumbbells or an EZ-bar.
execution_steps: Keeping your upper arms perfectly vertical and stationary, curl the weight up as high as possible.
Squeeze the biceps at peak contraction.
Lower the weight slowly to a full dead hang.
common_mistakes: Letting elbows drift backward as you lift
Using momentum by lifting the chest off the bench
Not fully extending at the bottom
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Place one hand and knee on a flat bench. With the other hand, hold a light dumbbell and bring your upper arm parallel to the floor.
execution_steps: Keep your upper arm pinned to your side.
Extend your elbow backward until your arm is completely straight.
Squeeze the triceps hard, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to a 90-degree angle.
common_mistakes: Using too much weight and sacrificing form
cues: Pin the elbow to the ribs
breathing_pattern: Exhale while kicking back, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Lie flat on a bench holding dumbbells directly above your chest with a pronated grip, dumbbells touching end-to-end.
execution_steps: Keeping your elbows flared out and stationary, hinge at the elbows to lower the inner edges of the dumbbells down toward your chest.
Stop right before they touch your chest, then use your triceps to press them back to the starting position.
Maintain control and proper breathing throughout the entire movement.
common_mistakes: Moving the shoulders instead of isolating the elbows
Letting the dumbbells crash into the chest
cues: Squeeze the triceps at the top
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Lie on a bench with a close grip on the barbell, elbows tucked 45 degrees.
execution_steps: Lower the bar toward your upper chest/neck area, allowing your elbows to track forward toward your feet, blending a close-grip bench press with a skull crusher.
Once the forearms touch the biceps, press the bar back up in a straight line.
Maintain control and proper breathing throughout the entire movement.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a pure skull crusher or pure close grip bench
Failing to let elbows track forward
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Place a mini resistance band around your ankles or just above your knees. Adopt a quarter-squat athletic stance.
execution_steps: Step laterally to one side, keeping tension on the band.
Slowly bring the trailing leg in, but do not let the band lose tension.
Repeat for desired reps, then switch directions.
common_mistakes: Standing straight up instead of staying in a squat
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously.

exercise_setup: Place your top foot/ankle on a bench and your bottom elbow on the floor (side plank position).
execution_steps: Press the top foot into the bench to lift your hips and bottom leg off the floor.
Your body should form a straight line.
Hold this isometric position, squeezing the inner thigh of the top leg.
common_mistakes: Bending the top knee (if performing the straight-leg version)
cues: Keep body in a straight line
breathing_pattern: Breathe steadily and rhythmically.

exercise_setup: Lie on your back with your lower back pressed into the floor. Place your hands lightly behind your head, elbows wide.
execution_steps: Lift your head, shoulders, and legs off the floor.
Bring your right knee toward your chest while simultaneously twisting your torso to bring your left elbow toward the right knee.
Extend the right leg while bringing the left knee in and twisting the right elbow to the left knee.
common_mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands
Rushing the movement and using momentum
Not fully extending the non-working leg
cues: Shoulder to knee, not elbow to knee
breathing_pattern: Exhale as you twist toward the knee, inhale as you transition.

exercise_setup: Secure your feet at the top of a decline bench. Lie back completely.
execution_steps: Place your hands across your chest or lightly behind your ears.
Flex your spine to crunch your torso upward, focusing on bringing your ribs to your pelvis.
Slowly lower your torso back down under control until you feel a stretch in the abs.
common_mistakes: Using momentum to throw the body up
Keeping the back flat instead of curling the spine
breathing_pattern: Exhale while crunching up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Set a bench to a low incline. Lie face down with your chest supported, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated (overhand) grip.
execution_steps: Flare your elbows out to 90 degrees.
Row the weights up by driving your elbows out and back.
Squeeze your rear delts at the top, then slowly lower the weights.
common_mistakes: Tucking the elbows in (shifts focus to lats)
Lifting the chest off the bench
cues: Squeeze the back of the shoulder
breathing_pattern: Exhale while rowing, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit on a bench with the balls of your feet on a block or weight plate. Rest a heavy dumbbell on top of each knee.
execution_steps: Lower your heels toward the floor until you feel a deep stretch in the calves.
Press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
Hold the squeeze at the top.
common_mistakes: Not getting a full stretch at the bottom
cues: Control the weight on the knees
breathing_pattern: Exhale while lifting heels, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand a few feet in front of a bench. Reach one foot back and rest the top of your foot on the bench. Hold dumbbells in each hand.
execution_steps: Keep your chest up and core braced. Lower your body until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Your back knee should hover just above the floor.
Drive through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Standing too close or too far from the bench
breathing_pattern: Inhale while descending, exhale while pushing up.

exercise_setup: Approach the barbell as if doing a deadlift. Hinge at the hips until your torso is strictly parallel to the floor.
execution_steps: Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Explosively pull the bar to your lower chest/upper stomach without raising your torso.
Return the bar completely to the floor for a dead stop before the next rep.
common_mistakes: Raising the torso during the pull (turning it into a standard bent-over row)
Bouncing the bar off the floor
Not letting the weight settle between reps
cues: Keep torso parallel to the floor
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace before pulling, exhale upon returning to the floor.

exercise_setup: Lie face down on an elevated flat bench (high enough so the plates don't hit the floor). Grab the barbell placed under the bench.
execution_steps: Pull the barbell straight up toward the underside of the bench.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower the bar back to a full dead hang.
common_mistakes: Lifting the head and chest off the bench
breathing_pattern: Exhale while rowing, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit on the floor with your legs straight out in front of you, spread in a V-shape. Hold a barbell at shoulder height.
execution_steps: Keep your torso perfectly upright using your core and hip flexors.
Press the barbell overhead to full lockout.
Lower the bar under control back to your shoulders without slouching.
common_mistakes: Leaning backward to press the weight
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pressing, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit in the machine and fasten the seatbelt if available. Place your elbows on the pads and grab the bar.
execution_steps: Pull the bar overhead and down toward your abdomen using only your lats and shoulders.
Squeeze at the bottom of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position until you feel a deep stretch in the lats.
common_mistakes: Using the triceps to push the bar
Lifting the lower back off the seat
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling down, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Kneel on a soft mat with your knees shoulder-width apart and your feet flat or toes tucked under. Keep your body in a straight line from knees to head.
execution_steps: Brace your core and glutes. Lean backward as far as you can while maintaining the straight line.
Use your quadriceps to stop the descent and pull yourself back up to the starting position.
Maintain control and proper breathing throughout the entire movement.
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips to lean back
cues: Straight line from knee to head
breathing_pattern: Inhale while leaning back, exhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Attach an ankle strap to a low cable pulley and put it on one ankle. Face the machine and hold the support beam.
execution_steps: Keeping your core braced and a slight bend in your working knee, kick your leg straight back.
Squeeze your glute hard at the peak.
Slowly return to the starting position without letting the weight stack rest.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back to get the leg higher
breathing_pattern: Exhale while kicking back, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Lie on your back on a flat bench with your head hanging off the edge. Place a folded towel and a light weight plate on your forehead, holding it with both hands.
execution_steps: Lower your head backward as far as comfortably possible to stretch the front of your neck.
Curl your head upward, bringing your chin toward your chest.
Slowly return to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Releasing the plate and letting it slip
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Lie face down on a flat bench with your head hanging off the edge. Place a towel and a light weight plate on the back of your head, holding it securely.
execution_steps: Lower your head down toward the floor to stretch the back of your neck.
Raise your head up and back, looking toward the wall in front of you.
Hold briefly and lower under control.
common_mistakes: Overextending the neck to the point of pain
breathing_pattern: Exhale while extending up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit on the floor or between parallettes with your legs straight out in front of you.
execution_steps: Place your hands on the floor/parallettes. Depress your shoulders, lock your elbows, and lift your hips and legs off the ground.
Keep your legs perfectly straight and parallel to the floor, forming an L shape with your body.
Hold this position for time.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging back behind the arms
Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously, using shallow breaths while bracing.

exercise_setup: Lie on your back on a flat bench and grip the edges of the bench firmly behind your head.
execution_steps: Raise your entire body (legs and torso) up until it is almost vertical, resting only on your upper shoulders.
Keeping your body in a perfectly straight line, slowly lower your legs and torso together toward the bench.
Stop just before touching, then raise back up.
common_mistakes: Bending the hips (turning it into a leg raise)
Arching the lower back excessively on the descent
Putting weight on the neck instead of the upper back
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pushing back up.

exercise_setup: Lie on your back, holding a kettlebell in your right hand straight up over your chest. Bend your right knee and plant the foot. Extend your left arm and leg out at a 45-degree angle.
execution_steps: Roll onto your left elbow, then push up to your left hand. Bridge your hips up.
Sweep your left leg under you into a kneeling position.
Stand up completely, keeping the kettlebell locked out overhead.
Reverse the exact sequence to return to the floor.
common_mistakes: Taking your eyes off the kettlebell
Bending the arm holding the weight
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously through each transition phase.

exercise_setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand. Hinge at the hips to swing the kettlebell back between your legs.
execution_steps: Explosively drive your hips forward to launch the kettlebell upward.
As the bell passes your chest, pull it close and punch your hand upward to catch it smoothly overhead.
Let the bell drop back down between your legs, absorbing the force with your hips.
common_mistakes: Letting the bell slam into the wrist
Using the shoulder to lift instead of the hips
Casting the bell too far forward on the drop
breathing_pattern: Inhale on the drop, exhale sharply on the hip snap.

exercise_setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with a false grip or standard overhand grip. Generate slight momentum.
execution_steps: Perform an explosive pull-up, pulling the bar down to your upper stomach.
Aggressively throw your chest and head forward over the bar to transition into a dip position.
Press out of the dip until your arms are fully extended.
common_mistakes: Chicken-winging (transitioning one arm at a time, highly dangerous for shoulders)
Not pulling high enough before the transition
breathing_pattern: Inhale before the pull, exhale on the dip press out.

exercise_setup: Sit in the machine and adjust the seat so the pivot point aligns with your shoulder joints. Place your arms against the pads and grip the handles.
execution_steps: Raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor.
Pause and squeeze the side delts.
Slowly lower the pads back to the starting position.
breathing_pattern: Exhale while raising, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Attach a D-handle to a high pulley. Sit or kneel facing the machine. Grab the handle with one hand.
execution_steps: Pull the handle down to your side, driving your elbow toward your hip.
Squeeze the lat intensely at the bottom.
Slowly let the handle pull your arm back up to a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the bicep instead of the lat
Not getting a full stretch at the top
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling, inhale while stretching.

exercise_setup: Secure your legs on a decline bench. Lie back holding a pair of dumbbells at your chest.
execution_steps: Press the dumbbells straight up until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, keeping your elbows tucked at roughly a 45-degree angle.
Feel the stretch in the lower chest.
common_mistakes: Flaring the elbows out to 90 degrees
Clanking the dumbbells together at the top
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pressing, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Clean and press a kettlebell or dumbbell overhead with one arm. Keep your elbow locked and bicep close to your ear.
execution_steps: Brace your core to prevent your ribs from flaring and lower back from arching.
Walk forward slowly and deliberately while balancing the weight directly overhead.
Maintain perfect upright posture.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back to compensate for poor shoulder mobility
breathing_pattern: Breathe rhythmically into a braced core.

exercise_setup: Hold light dumbbells in front of your thighs. Perform a wide upright row until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
execution_steps: Keeping your upper arms parallel to the floor, externally rotate your shoulders to flip the dumbbells up.
Press the dumbbells straight overhead.
Reverse the entire sequence slowly to return to the start.
breathing_pattern: Inhale on the row and rotation, exhale on the press.

exercise_setup: Stand on a box holding a light kettlebell or barbell. Keep your legs completely straight (knees locked).
execution_steps: Tuck your chin to your chest and slowly roll your spine downward, vertebrae by vertebrae.
Allow the weight to pull you into a deep hamstring and lower back stretch below the level of the box.
Slowly reverse the motion, unrolling the spine from the bottom up until you are standing tall.
common_mistakes: Using heavy weight (this is a mobility drill, not a strength lift)
Hinging at the hips instead of articulating the spine
breathing_pattern: Exhale as you roll down, inhale as you roll up.

exercise_setup: Sit in the machine and strap the belt securely across your hip crease. Plant your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform.
execution_steps: Drive through your heels to extend your hips fully.
Squeeze the glutes at the top of the movement.
Lower the weight under control until your hips are near the floor.
common_mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back instead of locking out the hips
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while thrusting up.

exercise_setup: Attach a straight bar or rope to a high pulley. Stand facing the machine, step back to create tension, and hinge slightly at the hips.
execution_steps: Keeping your arms straight (with a micro-bend in the elbows), pull the bar down in an arc to your thighs.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom.
Slowly return to the starting position until you feel a stretch in the lats.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows (turning it into a triceps pushdown)
cues: Sweep the bar to your pockets
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling down, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Start on all fours. Lift your knees an inch off the ground, keeping your back perfectly flat like a table.
execution_steps: Move your right hand and left foot forward simultaneously.
Then move your left hand and right foot forward.
Keep your hips low and avoid swaying side to side.
common_mistakes: Hips lifting too high (downward dog position)
Taking steps that are too large
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously and shallowly.

exercise_setup: Lie on your back with legs straight and arms extended overhead.
execution_steps: Press your lower back firmly into the floor by contracting your abs.
Lift your shoulders and legs slightly off the ground, creating a banana or hollow shape.
Hold this position, keeping the lower back glued to the floor.
common_mistakes: Lower back coming off the floor
cues: Crush the floor with your lower back
breathing_pattern: Breathe shallowly while keeping the core fully braced.

exercise_setup: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand. Brace your core.
execution_steps: Step backward with one leg, lowering your hips until both knees are bent at a 90-degree angle.
The back knee should hover just above the floor.
Drive through the heel of the front foot to return to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Slamming the back knee into the floor
breathing_pattern: Inhale while stepping back, exhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Stand on one leg. Lift the other foot off the ground and bend the knee so the foot is behind you.
execution_steps: Lower your body by bending the standing knee, reaching your arms forward for balance.
Touch your back knee lightly to the floor (or a pad) without letting the back foot touch.
Drive through your standing foot to return to the top.
common_mistakes: Letting the back foot touch the ground to assist the push
Knee valgus (caving in) on the working leg
Crashing the back knee into the floor
cues: Reach forward as you go down
breathing_pattern: Inhale on the way down, exhale on the way up.
progressions: Weighted Skater Squat (holding light DBs forward)
regressions: Skater Squat to a higher pad

exercise_setup: Sit in the machine and adjust the seat so your elbows align with the pivot point. Rest your triceps flat on the pad.
execution_steps: Grip the handles and curl the weight upward toward your shoulders.
Squeeze the biceps at the peak of the movement.
Lower the handles slowly until your arms are fully extended.
common_mistakes: Lifting the elbows off the pad
Using momentum by throwing the torso back
Not fully extending at the bottom
cues: Keep triceps glued to the pad
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit in the machine and adjust the seat so your elbows align with the pivot point. Rest your upper arms on the pad.
execution_steps: Grip the handles and push them downward or outward (depending on the machine design) until your arms are fully extended.
Squeeze the triceps hard.
Return slowly to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbows flare off the pad
Using body weight to press the handles
breathing_pattern: Exhale while extending, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Stand next to a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell. Hinge down and pick it up with one hand, keeping your back flat.
execution_steps: Stand perfectly upright. Brace your core to resist the weight pulling you to one side.
Walk forward with controlled, even steps.
Keep your shoulders level and do not lean away from the weight.
common_mistakes: Leaning away from the weight to compensate
Resting the weight against the leg
Shrugging the shoulder of the working arm
breathing_pattern: Breathe rhythmically into a braced core.

exercise_setup: Hold a kettlebell by the ''horns'' (sides of the handle) upside down in front of your chest.
execution_steps: Keeping the kettlebell close to your body, slowly circle it around your head.
Keep your core braced so your torso does not sway.
Complete a full circle back to the chest, then reverse the direction.
common_mistakes: Moving the head to get around the kettlebell instead of moving the arms
Using a weight that is too heavy
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously throughout the circle.

exercise_setup: Stand holding a resistance band in front of you with straight arms, hands shoulder-width apart. Overhand or underhand grip.
execution_steps: Keeping your arms straight, pull the band apart until it touches your chest.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together hard.
Slowly return to the starting position without letting the band lose all tension.
common_mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling apart, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Lie on your side with your hips and knees bent at 45 degrees, legs stacked. Rest your head on your lower arm.
execution_steps: Keeping your feet touching, raise your top knee as high as you can without rolling your pelvis backward.
Squeeze the side of your glute at the top.
Lower the knee slowly back down.
common_mistakes: Rolling the hips backward to get the knee higher
breathing_pattern: Exhale while opening the knee, inhale while closing.

exercise_setup: Adjust the chest pad and position yourself in the machine (standing or kneeling depending on the design). Place one foot on the push plate.
execution_steps: Drive the plate backward by extending your hip.
Squeeze the glute forcefully at the end of the movement.
Slowly let the leg return to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back to extend the leg further
breathing_pattern: Exhale while kicking back, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Stand holding the loaded end of a landmine barbell at chest height with both hands, fingers interlaced. Lean slightly forward into the bar.
execution_steps: Squat down by sitting your hips back and bending your knees.
Keep your chest up and core tight.
Drive through your feet to stand back up, pushing slightly into the bar.
common_mistakes: Standing too far away and leaning too much
breathing_pattern: Inhale while descending, exhale while ascending.

exercise_setup: Stand with your back against a wall. Walk your feet out and slide down until your hips and knees are both at 90-degree angles.
execution_steps: Keep your back flat against the wall and your weight in your heels.
Hold this seated position for the desired amount of time.
Do not rest your hands on your thighs.
common_mistakes: Resting hands on the legs to cheat
Sliding feet too close to the wall (knees over toes awkwardly)
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously and evenly.

exercise_setup: Stand inside a trap bar and deadlift it up to a standing position.
execution_steps: Keeping your arms perfectly straight, shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Hold the contraction at the top.
Lower the bar back to a full stretch without bending your arms or rounding your back.
breathing_pattern: Exhale while shrugging, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Attach a rope to a high pulley. Stand facing away from the machine, holding the rope ends behind your neck.
execution_steps: Hinge slightly at the hips to start.
Flex your spine, crunching your torso down and bringing your elbows toward your knees.
Slowly return to the starting position without hyperextending your back.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms instead of the abs
Flexing at the hips instead of the spine
Arching the lower back on the return
breathing_pattern: Exhale while crunching down, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, a dumbbell on the floor between your feet. Hinge down and grab it with one hand.
execution_steps: Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles.
As the dumbbell flies upward, pull it close to your body and quickly punch your hand under it to catch it overhead with a straight arm.
Lower the dumbbell safely back to the floor.
common_mistakes: Pressing the weight out instead of using momentum
Letting the dumbbell swing far away from the body
cues: Keep it close like zipping a jacket
breathing_pattern: Inhale before the pull, exhale as you punch overhead.

exercise_setup: Get on all fours on a mat, hands under shoulders and knees under hips. Keep your back flat.
execution_steps: Keeping your right knee bent at 90 degrees, lift your right leg and press your heel toward the ceiling.
Squeeze your glute at the top of the movement.
Lower the knee back down without letting it touch the ground.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back to get the leg higher
cues: Press the heel to the ceiling
breathing_pattern: Exhale while lifting the leg, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Hold a wrist roller device with both hands straight out in front of you at shoulder height (or resting on a rack).
execution_steps: Roll the weight up by alternately flexing/extending your wrists, winding the rope around the dowel.
Once the weight reaches the top, slowly unroll it back down under control.
Repeat by rolling in the opposite direction (flexion vs extension).
common_mistakes: Letting the weight free-fall on the way down
Dropping the arms because the shoulders get tired
cues: Keep arms parallel to the floor
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously.
regressions: Rest arms on a rack to eliminate shoulder fatigue

exercise_setup: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat on the sliders/towels. Bridge your hips up.
execution_steps: Keeping your hips bridged high, slowly slide your feet out until your legs are nearly straight.
Dig your heels into the sliders and pull your feet back toward your glutes.
Maintain the hip bridge throughout the entire movement.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips sag toward the floor as the legs extend
breathing_pattern: Inhale as you slide out, exhale as you curl back.

exercise_setup: Set a cable pulley to chest/shoulder height. Stand sideways to the machine, reaching across your torso to grab the cable (no attachment needed, grab the ball/stopper).
execution_steps: Keep your upper arm pinned to your side or slightly elevated.
Extend your elbow across your body until your arm is fully straight.
Squeeze the triceps and slowly return to the stretched position across your chest.
common_mistakes: Using torso rotation to pull the weight
Standing too close and losing tension
breathing_pattern: Exhale while extending, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Set a cable pulley to the lowest position. Stand sideways to the machine, hinge slightly, and grab the handle with both hands.
execution_steps: Keeping your arms relatively straight, pull the handle diagonally upward and across your body.
Pivot your back foot and rotate your torso.
Slowly reverse the motion back to the low starting point.
common_mistakes: Using only the arms (front raise) instead of rotating
Keeping feet planted firmly without pivoting
breathing_pattern: Exhale while chopping up, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a non-bouncing medicine ball.
execution_steps: Reach the ball high overhead, extending your hips and coming up onto your toes.
Explosively throw the ball straight down into the floor, hinging at the hips and crunching your abs.
Catch the ball on the bounce or pick it up to repeat.
common_mistakes: Arching the back excessively at the top
Throwing with just the arms instead of using the core
Using a bouncy ball and getting hit in the face
breathing_pattern: Inhale as you reach up, exhale forcefully as you slam.

exercise_setup: Stand over a kettlebell. Hinge down and grip the handle with one hand.
execution_steps: Swing the kettlebell back between your legs to generate momentum.
Explosively drive your hips forward and pull the kettlebell upward.
Keep the bell close to your body and quickly rotate your wrist to catch the kettlebell softly in the rack position at your chest.
Drop it back down into the swing.
common_mistakes: Casting the kettlebell out away from the body
Letting it slam painfully into the forearm
Curling the weight instead of using hip power
breathing_pattern: Inhale on the drop, exhale on the catch.

exercise_setup: Press a kettlebell overhead with your right arm. Point both feet 45 degrees to the left. Keep your right leg perfectly straight.
execution_steps: Looking up at the kettlebell, push your right hip out to the side.
Hinge at the hips and slide your left hand down your left leg toward the floor.
Go as low as your mobility allows without bending the right knee.
Squeeze your glutes and core to stand back up.
common_mistakes: Bending the knee of the loaded side
Taking your eyes off the kettlebell
breathing_pattern: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you stand.

exercise_setup: Set up exactly like a standard barbell hip thrust. Stagger your feet: keep the working foot flat on the floor, and step the non-working foot slightly forward, resting only on the heel/toes for balance.
execution_steps: Drive through the heel of the working leg to thrust the barbell upward.
The staggered foot should provide only 10-20% of the effort for balance.
Squeeze the glute of the working leg hard at the top.
Lower under control.
breathing_pattern: Inhale before the thrust, exhale at the top.

exercise_setup: Stand tall holding a pair of dumbbells by your sides with a neutral grip.
execution_steps: With a slight bend in your elbows, raise the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Pour the water out of the pitchers slightly at the top (internally rotate wrists).
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Using momentum by swinging the torso
Shrugging the traps to lift the weight
Raising the weights above shoulder level
breathing_pattern: Exhale while raising, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand on the edge of a block or step with one foot. Hold a dumbbell in the same-side hand, and hold onto a wall/rack with the other hand for balance. Tuck the non-working leg behind you.
execution_steps: Lower your heel as far as possible to stretch the calf.
Push through the ball of your foot to raise your heel as high as possible.
Squeeze the calf at the peak.
common_mistakes: Not going through a full range of motion
