breathing_pattern: Exhale while raising, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Lie on your back on a mat. Bend your knees to 90 degrees and lift your feet off the floor. Place your hands by your sides or hold onto a heavy object behind your head.
execution_steps: Contract your abs to curl your hips off the floor, bringing your knees toward your chest.
Squeeze the abs hard at the top.
Slowly lower your hips back to the floor without letting your lower back arch.
common_mistakes: Using momentum by kicking the legs
Not lifting the pelvis off the floor (only moving the hips)
Letting the lower back arch at the bottom
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Hang from a pull-up bar. Lift your legs straight up until your feet are near the bar (pike position).
execution_steps: Keeping your legs perfectly straight and pressed together, rotate your hips to sweep your legs to the right side like a windshield wiper.
Control the momentum, then sweep them all the way across to the left side.
Maintain tension in your lats and core to avoid swinging wildly.
common_mistakes: Dropping the legs out of the pike position
breathing_pattern: Breathe shallowly but continuously during the movement.

exercise_setup: Sit on a Swiss ball, then walk your feet forward and roll down until your lower and mid-back are supported by the curve of the ball. Plant feet firmly.
execution_steps: With hands behind your head or crossed on your chest, stretch your abs over the contour of the ball.
Contract your abs to crunch your torso upward.
Slowly lower back down, feeling a deep stretch in the abdominals.
common_mistakes: Rolling the ball instead of crunching the spine
Not getting a full stretch at the bottom
breathing_pattern: Exhale while crunching, inhale while stretching.

exercise_setup: Lie face down on an incline bench holding heavy dumbbells. Pull the dumbbells up as high as possible, retracting the shoulder blades.
execution_steps: Hold the peak contraction (the batwing position) for a full 3-5 seconds.
Squeeze the rhomboids and mid-traps as hard as possible.
Lower the dumbbells completely, let the scapula stretch, and repeat.
common_mistakes: Not holding the squeeze long enough
Using weight that is too heavy to hold at the top
Lifting the chest off the bench
breathing_pattern: Exhale on the pull, breathe shallowly during the hold, inhale on the release.

exercise_setup: Lie face down on an incline bench holding dumbbells. Let your arms hang straight down, completely relaxing your shoulder blades so they stretch forward (protraction).
execution_steps: Keeping your arms perfectly straight, pinch your shoulder blades together as hard as possible to lift the weight.
Hold the squeeze for a second.
Lower the weight back to a full dead stretch.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows (turning it into a row)
cues: Pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
breathing_pattern: Exhale while retracting, inhale while protracting.

exercise_setup: Set up like a standard single-arm dumbbell row, but use a much heavier dumbbell. Plant one hand and knee on a bench.
execution_steps: Use a slight amount of body english (momentum) from the torso and legs to initiate the pull.
Row the massive dumbbell forcefully to your chest/ribcage.
Control the descent somewhat, but focus on moving heavy weight for high reps (15-20+).
common_mistakes: Using so much momentum that the lats are completely bypassed
cues: Let it stretch at the bottom
breathing_pattern: Breathe forcefully and rhythmically.

exercise_setup: Lie on a flat bench. Grip the barbell with a supinated (underhand) grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width. (Highly recommended to use a spotter to unrack).
execution_steps: Unrack the bar and lower it to your lower chest/upper abs.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your body.
Press the bar up and back in a slight arc until your arms are fully extended.
common_mistakes: Not using a spotter for the unrack (highly dangerous for wrists)
Lowering the bar too high on the chest
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Stand with your heels elevated on a wedge or weight plates, feet close together (narrow stance). Hold a dumbbell in the goblet position.
execution_steps: Keeping your torso extremely upright, squat down deeply, letting your knees track far forward over your toes.
Go as deep as your mobility allows, attempting to touch hamstrings to calves.
Drive through your quads to stand back up.
common_mistakes: Pushing the hips far back like a standard squat
Not going deep enough to bias the teardrop quad muscle
breathing_pattern: Inhale while descending, exhale while ascending.

exercise_setup: Lie flat on your back with legs straight and arms extended overhead on the floor.
execution_steps: Simultaneously lift your straight legs and your torso off the floor.
Reach your hands toward your toes, balancing on your tailbone to form a V shape.
Slowly lower your arms and legs back to the floor without letting them completely rest.
common_mistakes: Not lifting the torso (just doing a leg raise)
Using momentum to throw the body up
breathing_pattern: Exhale as you fold up, inhale as you lower.

exercise_setup: Sit on a flat bench with your feet planted wide apart. Unrack a barbell and place it across your upper back.
execution_steps: Keeping your back perfectly flat and chest up, hinge forward at the hips.
Lower your torso between your legs as far as your mobility allows.
Use your lower back and glutes to pull your torso back to the upright position.
common_mistakes: Looking down instead of keeping a neutral neck
cues: Feel the stretch in the groin and lower back
breathing_pattern: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you return upright.

exercise_setup: Place an incline bench between two low cable pulleys. Grab the handles and lie back on the bench.
execution_steps: With a slight bend in your elbows, pull the handles up and together in an arc until they meet above your upper chest.
Squeeze the upper chest hard.
Slowly lower the handles back down until you feel a stretch across your chest.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows into a press
Going too heavy and tearing the shoulder capsule at the bottom
Lifting the head off the bench
breathing_pattern: Exhale while bringing the cables together, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Loop a heavy resistance band around a sturdy rig and step inside it, placing the band behind both knees. Step back to create high tension.
execution_steps: Sit back into a squat position, keeping your shins perfectly vertical.
Let the band support your weight while your quads work to keep your knees extended against the band.
Hold this position for the desired time.
common_mistakes: Not using a heavy enough band
breathing_pattern: Breathe rhythmically.

exercise_setup: Stand with a very wide stance, toes pointed slightly outward.
execution_steps: Shift your weight to the right leg, bending the right knee and pushing the hips back.
Keep the left leg completely straight and let the left toes point up toward the ceiling (rotating on the heel).
Go as deep as your mobility allows, then push back to the center and repeat on the other side.
common_mistakes: Heel of the bent leg coming off the floor
Not rotating the straight leg's toes up
breathing_pattern: Inhale as you descend, exhale as you push up.

exercise_setup: Stand tall holding dumbbells by your sides.
execution_steps: Step your right foot behind and across your left leg (like a curtsy).
Bend both knees to lower your hips until your left thigh is parallel to the floor.
Drive through the left heel to return to the starting position, then switch sides.
common_mistakes: Taking a step that is too wide or too narrow
breathing_pattern: Inhale as you step back, exhale as you return.

exercise_setup: Load a sled with plates. Grip the high or low handles with straight arms. Lean your torso forward.
execution_steps: Drive your legs into the ground, taking powerful, rhythmic steps to push the sled forward.
Keep your core braced and spine neutral.
Continue for the desired distance.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows and losing power transfer
Taking steps that are too short/choppy
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously and heavily.

exercise_setup: Attach straps to a sled and hold them, or wear a harness. Face away from the sled (or toward it for reverse drag). For reverse drag: face the sled, hold straps with arms straight.
execution_steps: Lean back slightly, keeping tension on the straps.
Take deliberate steps backward, driving through your toes and fully extending your knees to pull the sled.
Maintain a braced core and upright posture.
common_mistakes: Jerking the sled with the arms instead of using the legs
Standing too upright and losing leverage
Taking steps that are too large
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously.

exercise_setup: Lie on your side with your legs straight. Prop your upper body up on your forearm, with your elbow directly under your shoulder.
execution_steps: Brace your core and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from ankles to shoulders.
Hold this position, preventing your hips from sagging toward the floor.
Keep your neck neutral.
cues: Push the floor away with the elbow
breathing_pattern: Breathe rhythmically.
progressions: Side Plank with Leg Lift (Star Plank)

exercise_setup: Get into a standard side plank position on your forearm or hand.
execution_steps: Once stable, lift your top leg straight up into the air (hip abduction).
Simultaneously reach your top arm straight toward the ceiling.
Hold this star shape, keeping the hips high and body aligned.
common_mistakes: Hips dropping immediately upon lifting the leg
breathing_pattern: Breathe rhythmically into a braced core.

exercise_setup: Kneel on a mat with your forearms resting on a Swiss ball in front of you.
execution_steps: Keeping your core braced and your body in a straight line from knees to head, slowly roll the ball forward.
Extend your arms as far as you can without letting your lower back sag.
Use your core and lats to pull the ball back to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Hinging at the hips (sticking the butt out) instead of rolling the whole body
breathing_pattern: Inhale while rolling out, exhale while pulling back.

exercise_setup: Lie on your back with your arms extended toward the ceiling and your knees bent at 90 degrees (shins parallel to the floor).
execution_steps: Press your lower back firmly into the floor.
Slowly lower your right arm and left leg toward the floor simultaneously.
Stop just before they touch the ground, keeping your lower back glued to the floor.
Return to the starting position and repeat with the opposite arm and leg.
common_mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor
Moving the same side arm and leg
cues: Crush the floor with your lower back
breathing_pattern: Inhale as limbs go down, exhale as they come up.

exercise_setup: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips. Keep your back flat like a table.
execution_steps: Simultaneously extend your right arm straight forward and your left leg straight backward.
Reach long through the fingertips and heel, squeezing the glute and back.
Avoid rotating your hips or arching your lower back.
Return to the start and switch sides.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back to lift the leg higher
Twisting the hips to the side
Looking up and straining the neck
cues: Keep a glass of water on your back
breathing_pattern: Inhale as you extend, exhale as you return.
progressions: Bird Dog from a high plank position

exercise_setup: Grab the TRX handles and get into a push-up position. Walk your feet back to increase the angle and difficulty. Brace your core.
execution_steps: Lower your body by bending your elbows, letting them track at about a 45-degree angle.
Go as deep as you comfortably can, feeling a stretch in the chest.
Press back up to the starting position, keeping the straps from rubbing your arms.
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Place your hands on parallettes, weight plates, or hex dumbbells slightly wider than shoulder-width. Get into a push-up position.
execution_steps: Lower your body, allowing your chest to go below the level of your hands to achieve a deep stretch in the pecs.
Pause briefly at the bottom.
Press forcefully back up to lockout.
common_mistakes: Going too deep and straining the shoulder capsule
cues: Deep stretch, but don't force pain
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Stand holding very light weight plates or dumbbells by your sides.
execution_steps: Keeping your arms straight, raise the weights out to the sides.
Continue raising them past parallel all the way until they touch overhead.
Slowly lower them back down through the same wide arc.
common_mistakes: Using heavy weight (this requires light weight)
Arching the lower back at the top
breathing_pattern: Exhale while raising, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand beside the Smith machine bar. Hinge at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Grab the bar with one hand.
execution_steps: Row the bar up toward your hip/ribcage, keeping your elbow tucked.
Squeeze your lat at the top.
Lower the bar back down to a full stretch. The Smith machine fixes the bar path, allowing you to focus entirely on the muscle.
common_mistakes: Pulling toward the chest instead of the hip
breathing_pattern: Exhale while rowing, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Set a low cable pulley. Stand slightly in front of it and reach behind your back to grab the handle with the opposite hand.
execution_steps: Keeping a slight bend in your elbow, raise the handle out to the side until it reaches shoulder height.
Squeeze the lateral delt.
Slowly lower it back behind your body, feeling a deep stretch across the shoulder.
common_mistakes: Pulling the cable in front of the body
cues: Keep the cable close to the glutes
breathing_pattern: Exhale while raising, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley. Lie flat on your back on the floor, with your feet bracing against the machine.
execution_steps: Keeping your elbows pinned to the floor and upper arms stationary, curl the bar toward your chest.
Squeeze the biceps hard.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position. Lying down prevents any body english (momentum).
common_mistakes: Lifting the elbows off the floor
Lifting the head off the floor
cues: Pin the elbows to the ground
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand holding a barbell with an underhand grip, resting against your thighs.
execution_steps: Instead of curling the bar in an arc, drag the bar straight up your torso.
To do this, you must pull your elbows back behind your body as you flex them.
Squeeze the biceps at the top, then drag the bar back down.
common_mistakes: Curling the bar away from the body (turning it into a standard curl)
breathing_pattern: Exhale while dragging up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley. Grab the bar with a supinated (underhand) grip, palms facing up.
execution_steps: Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
Push the bar down until your arms are fully extended.
Squeeze the triceps, then slowly return to the starting position. The underhand grip forces strict form and prevents you from pressing with your chest/shoulders.
common_mistakes: Letting the wrists bend backward excessively
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pushing down, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Attach a rope to a low or mid pulley. Turn away from the machine, grab the rope, and bring your hands behind your head.
execution_steps: Adopt a staggered stance and lean forward slightly.
Keeping your elbows pointing forward and stationary, extend your arms straight out.
Squeeze the triceps, then control the weight back down to a deep stretch behind the head.
common_mistakes: Flaring elbows out to the sides
breathing_pattern: Exhale while extending, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Stand with your back against a wall. Walk your feet forward about 1-2 feet. Keep your legs straight.
execution_steps: Keeping your heels on the ground, flex your ankles to pull your toes up toward your shins as high as possible.
Squeeze the muscle on the front of your shin (tibialis anterior).
Lower your toes slowly back to the ground.
common_mistakes: Not pulling the toes high enough
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously.
progressions: Walk feet further away from the wall (increases difficulty)
regressions: Walk feet closer to the wall

exercise_setup: Attach a straight bar to a low cable pulley. Stand facing the machine, holding the bar with an overhand grip.
execution_steps: Pull the bar straight up along the front of your body until it reaches chest height.
Lead with your elbows, keeping them higher than your wrists.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Pulling the bar too high (above the chest) causing shoulder impingement
cues: Keep the bar close to your body
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand facing a sturdy plyo box, about a foot away. Feet shoulder-width apart.
execution_steps: Swing your arms back and hinge slightly at the hips and knees to gather power.
Explosively jump up and forward onto the box, using your arm swing for momentum.
Land softly on the box with both feet in a partial squat. Step down carefully.
common_mistakes: Landing with straight legs or a loud thud
Jumping down backward (high risk for Achilles tear)
Using a box that is too high
breathing_pattern: Inhale before the jump, exhale mid-air or upon landing.

exercise_setup: Hold a barbell in the front rack position, resting on your shoulders. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
execution_steps: Perform a full front squat, descending until your hips are below your knees.
Explosively stand up from the squat.
Use the momentum from your legs to seamlessly press the barbell overhead until your arms are fully locked out.
common_mistakes: Pressing the bar before the hips are fully extended
Dropping the chest during the squat
Pausing at the shoulders between the squat and press
breathing_pattern: Inhale on the squat, exhale forcefully on the press.

exercise_setup: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
execution_steps: Drop into a squat position and place your hands on the floor.
Kick your feet back to a plank position and perform a push-up (chest to floor).
Quickly jump your feet back to the squat position.
Explosively jump into the air, reaching your arms overhead.
common_mistakes: Letting the lower back sag during the plank/push-up
Skipping the push-up (unless doing a half-burpee)
Landing heavily on the final jump
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously, matching the rhythm of the movement.

exercise_setup: Hold the ends of a battle rope with an overhand grip. Adopt a quarter-squat athletic stance, bracing your core.
execution_steps: Rapidly alternate whipping your arms up and down to create waves that travel all the way to the anchor point.
Keep your torso stable and do not let your hips bounce up and down.
Maintain control and proper breathing throughout the entire movement.
common_mistakes: Losing core tension and letting the body sway
breathing_pattern: Breathe rapidly and continuously.

exercise_setup: Set the weight stack to provide the desired amount of assistance (more weight = easier). Kneel on the pad and grip the overhead handles.
execution_steps: Pull your body up until your chin clears the bar, squeezing your lats.
Control your descent back to a full dead hang, letting the machine pad support your knees/feet.
Maintain control and proper breathing throughout the entire movement.
common_mistakes: Not getting a full stretch at the bottom
Shrugging the shoulders at the top
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Set the assistance weight (more weight = easier). Kneel on the pad and grip the parallel bars with arms locked out.
execution_steps: Lower your body by bending your elbows to 90 degrees.
Keep your elbows tucked slightly to target the triceps.
Press back up to full lockout.
common_mistakes: Going too deep and straining the shoulder
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Lie face down on a bench or the floor. Have a partner place a dumbbell between your arches/heels, or secure it yourself before lying down.
execution_steps: Squeeze the dumbbell securely between your feet.
Curl the weight up by flexing your knees until your shins are past perpendicular.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back down without letting it rest on the floor.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back to lift the weight
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Attach a bar or rope to a low pulley. Stand facing away from the machine with the cable running between your legs (or face the machine).
execution_steps: Keeping your arms straight with a micro-bend in the elbows, raise the attachment in front of you until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Squeeze the front delts.
Slowly return to the starting position without losing tension.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to cheat the weight up
breathing_pattern: Exhale while raising, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell on the floor with an overhand grip.
execution_steps: Explosively extend your hips and knees to pull the bar high, dropping quickly under it to catch it in the front rack position (the Clean).
From the rack position, immediately dip slightly and explosively press the bar overhead to full lockout (the Press).
Control the bar back to the shoulders, then safely to the floor.
common_mistakes: Curling the bar instead of using hip power
Pressing the bar out in front instead of straight up
Rounding the lower back off the floor
breathing_pattern: Inhale before the pull, exhale forcefully on the press overhead.

exercise_setup: Sit in the machine with your back flat against the pad. Place your feet shoulder-width apart in the middle of the sled.
execution_steps: Unrack the sled. Lower it by bending your knees and hips until your legs form a 90-degree angle (or as deep as your mobility allows without your lower back rounding).
Drive through your entire foot to push the sled back up, stopping just short of locking your knees.
Maintain control and proper breathing throughout the entire movement.
common_mistakes: Locking the knees forcefully at the top
Letting the lower back round off the pad at the bottom (butt wink)
cues: Keep lower back glued to the pad
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

primary_muscles: Quadriceps (Rectus Femoris, Vastus Lateralis, Vastus Medialis, Vastus Intermedius)
exercise_setup: Sit in the machine. Adjust the pad so it rests on your lower shins just above the feet. Adjust the backrest so your knees align with the machine's pivot point.
execution_steps: Grip the handles tightly. Extend your knees to lift the pad until your legs are fully straight.
Squeeze your quads hard at the top.
Slowly lower the weight back to the starting position without letting the plates crash.
common_mistakes: Using momentum by kicking the weight up
Lifting the glutes off the seat
breathing_pattern: Exhale while extending, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit on the bench with your feet on the footplates, knees slightly bent. Grab the V-bar with both hands and sit up tall with a flat back.
execution_steps: Pull the handle to your lower stomach by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the chest.
Control the weight back, allowing your shoulder blades to stretch forward without rounding your lower back.
common_mistakes: Using excessive torso momentum (leaning far back)
Pulling with the biceps instead of the back
cues: Squeeze a pencil between your shoulder blades
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling, inhale while releasing.

exercise_setup: Place one knee and the same-side hand on a flat bench. Keep your back flat and parallel to the floor. Hold a dumbbell in the free hand.
execution_steps: Pull the dumbbell straight up toward your hip/ribcage, keeping your elbow relatively close to your side.
Squeeze your back muscles at the top.
Lower the dumbbell under control until your arm is fully extended and you feel a stretch in the lat.
common_mistakes: Pulling the dumbbell to the chest instead of the hip
cues: Let the scapula stretch at the bottom
breathing_pattern: Exhale while rowing, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit on a flat bench with dumbbells resting on your thighs. Kick the weights up with your knees as you lie back.
execution_steps: Hold the dumbbells over your chest with arms fully extended, palms facing forward.
Lower the dumbbells under control until they are roughly level with your chest, elbows tucked at a 45-degree angle.
Press the weights forcefully back to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Clanking the dumbbells together at the top
Lifting the glutes off the bench
cues: Squeeze the chest at the top
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Set a bench to a 30-45 degree incline. Kick the dumbbells up to your shoulders and lie back.
execution_steps: Press the dumbbells straight up over your upper chest.
Lower the dumbbells slowly until you feel a deep stretch in the upper pecs.
Press the weights back to the top, squeezing the chest.
common_mistakes: Setting the bench too high (turns it into a shoulder press)
cues: Press straight up over the collarbone
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Set a cable pulley to upper chest or face height. Grab the rope with a neutral or overhand grip.
execution_steps: Pull the rope toward your face, letting your elbows flare outward and pulling your hands apart.
As the rope nears your face, externally rotate your shoulders so your hands go back past your ears (like a double bicep pose).
Squeeze your upper back, then slowly return to the start.
common_mistakes: Pulling to the neck instead of the face
Using too much weight and leaning back
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Stand holding a barbell with an overhand grip, feet shoulder-width apart. Keep a slight, fixed bend in your knees.
execution_steps: Hinge at the hips, pushing your glutes backward to lower the bar along your thighs.
Keep your back perfectly straight and your lats engaged. Lower until you feel a deep stretch in the hamstrings (usually just below the knees).
Drive your hips forward to stand back up, squeezing the glutes.
common_mistakes: Bending the knees too much (turning it into a squat)
Letting the bar drift away from the legs
cues: Shave your legs with the bar
Push hips to the wall behind you
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace while hinging down, exhale while standing up.

exercise_setup: Lie perpendicular across a flat bench with your upper back resting on it. Hold a single dumbbell with both hands (diamond grip under the top plate) directly over your chest.
execution_steps: Keeping your arms relatively straight with a slight elbow bend, lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head.
Lower until you feel a deep stretch in your lats and chest.
Pull the dumbbell back over your chest in the same arc.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows into a triceps extension
breathing_pattern: Inhale deeply while lowering, exhale while pulling back over.

exercise_setup: Adjust the seat height so the handles align with your mid-chest. Sit with your back flat against the pad.
execution_steps: Grip the handles and press them forward until your arms are fully extended.
Squeeze your chest at the top.
Slowly lower the handles back until you feel a stretch in your chest, without letting the weight stack rest.
common_mistakes: Lifting the lower back off the pad
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pressing, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Strap the belt around your hips and attach it to the machine's carriage. Stand on the platform with feet shoulder-width apart.
execution_steps: Squat down by bending your knees and hips, keeping your torso upright.
Go as deep as your mobility allows.
Drive through your feet to stand back up. The load is placed entirely on the hips, completely deloading the spine.
common_mistakes: Standing too far forward or back on the platform
breathing_pattern: Inhale while descending, exhale while ascending.

exercise_setup: Position your back flat against the pad and shoulders under the yokes. Place your feet on the platform.
execution_steps: Lower the machine by bending your knees. The pendulum arc allows you to squat extremely deep while maintaining an upright torso.
Squat until your hamstrings touch your calves (if mobility permits).
Drive through the platform to stand back up.
common_mistakes: Lifting the heels off the platform
Letting the lower back round off the pad
breathing_pattern: Inhale while descending, exhale while ascending.

exercise_setup: Set a bench to a 30-45 degree incline. Lie face down with your chest supported by the pad. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms hanging straight down.
execution_steps: Pull the dumbbells up toward your ribcage by driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower the dumbbells slowly to a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad
Pulling too high into the armpits (engages traps instead of lats/mid-back)
breathing_pattern: Exhale while rowing, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Adjust the seat height so the chest pad hits your mid-chest. Sit and grab the handles (perform one arm at a time for better focus, or both).
execution_steps: Pull the handle back toward your torso, squeezing the lat and upper back.
Keep your chest pressed against the pad.
Control the weight back to a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso off the pad to cheat the weight
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Get into a push-up position. Place your hands close together under your chest (forming a diamond shape with index fingers and thumbs is optional).
execution_steps: Keeping your body in a straight line, lower your chest toward your hands.
Keep your elbows tucked tightly to your sides to maximize triceps engagement.
Press forcefully back up to full elbow lockout.
common_mistakes: Flaring elbows out (puts extreme stress on wrists)
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Stand next to a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell. Feet shoulder-width apart.
execution_steps: Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the weight with one hand.
Keeping your core highly braced to prevent your torso from twisting or leaning, drive through the floor to stand up straight.
Lower the weight back to the floor under control.
common_mistakes: Leaning heavily toward the weight side
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace before lifting, exhale at the top.
regressions: Suitcase Deadlift off a block (shorter ROM)

exercise_setup: Set up exactly like a barbell hip thrust on a bench.
execution_steps: Instead of a full range of motion, drop your hips only a few inches (keeping tension entirely on the glutes).
Thrust back up and squeeze the glutes intensely at lockout.
This shortened ROM minimizes quad and hamstring involvement.
common_mistakes: Doing a full hip thrust (which engages more quads/hamstrings)
breathing_pattern: Inhale on the slight drop, exhale on the squeeze.

exercise_setup: Get into a standard forearm plank position with a slightly wider foot stance for balance.
execution_steps: Brace your core to lock your hips in place.
Slowly reach one arm straight out in front of you.
Hold for a second, return the arm, and alternate to the other side.
Do not let your hips twist or sway as you lift the arm.
common_mistakes: Hips aggressively twisting side to side
cues: Imagine a glass of water on your back
breathing_pattern: Breathe rhythmically.

exercise_setup: Lie face down on a 45-degree incline bench holding light dumbbells. Let arms hang straight down with thumbs pointing up.
execution_steps: Keeping your arms straight, raise them up and out at a 45-degree angle to form a Y shape with your body.
Squeeze your lower traps at the top.
Slowly lower back to the start.
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest off the bench
breathing_pattern: Exhale while raising, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand at the machine, adjusting the roller pad to sit just above your heel. Brace your torso against the support pads.
execution_steps: Curl the pad upward by flexing your knee as far as possible.
Squeeze the hamstring forcefully at the peak.
Slowly lower the pad back to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back to cheat the weight up
cues: Keep hips pressed into the pad
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Place one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment. Straddle the bar facing away from the landmine. Hook a V-grip handle under the bar near the loaded plates. Hinge at the hips.
execution_steps: Keeping your back flat and core braced, pull the bar up toward your chest by driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower the bar back down to a full stretch without letting it touch the ground.
common_mistakes: Standing too upright (turning it into a shrug)
Jerking the weight with the lower back
breathing_pattern: Exhale while rowing, inhale while lowering.
regressions: Chest-Supported T-Bar Row (saves the lower back)

exercise_setup: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand. Take a large step forward with one foot and plant it securely. Keep your rear foot stationary, resting on the ball of the foot.
execution_steps: Lower your hips straight down until both knees are bent at a 90-degree angle.
The rear knee should hover just above the floor.
Drive through the heel of the front foot to push straight back up to the starting staggered stance.
common_mistakes: Stepping too narrow (like walking on a tightrope)
Letting the front knee cave inward
Leaning too far forward over the front toes
cues: Drop straight down like an elevator
breathing_pattern: Inhale while descending, exhale while ascending.

exercise_setup: Place your feet on a bench or box and your hands on the floor, slightly wider than shoulder-width. Your body should form a straight line angling downward.
execution_steps: Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows.
Keep your core braced so your hips don't sag.
Press forcefully back up to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Looking up and straining the neck
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Start in a downward dog or push-up position, then walk your feet closer to your hands while keeping your legs straight. Your body should form an inverted V shape.
execution_steps: Lower the top of your head toward the floor slightly in front of your hands (creating a triangle with your hands and head).
Keep your elbows tucked in.
Press back up to the starting inverted V position, pushing your head back between your shoulders.
common_mistakes: Flaring elbows out to the sides
Lowering the head straight down between the hands instead of forward
cues: Form a tripod with hands and head
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Kick up into a handstand against a wall (heels touching the wall). Place your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, fingers pointing slightly outward.
execution_steps: Lower your body under control until your head touches the mat (or a deficit block).
Keep your elbows pointing forward at a 45-degree angle, not flared directly out to the sides.
Press powerfully back up to full elbow lockout.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back excessively (banana back)
Crashing the head into the floor
breathing_pattern: Inhale deeply at the top, hold while lowering, exhale while pressing.

contraindications: Lumbar disc herniation (if performed with poor form)
exercise_setup: Lie flat on your back on a mat. Place your hands under your glutes or by your sides. Keep your legs completely straight.
execution_steps: Press your lower back firmly into the floor.
Lift both legs up until they are perpendicular to the floor.
Slowly lower your legs back down, stopping just before they touch the floor or as soon as you feel your lower back arching.
common_mistakes: Letting the lower back arch completely off the floor on the descent
Using momentum to swing the legs up
cues: Crush the floor with your lower back
breathing_pattern: Exhale while lifting the legs, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Start in a high plank (push-up) position, hands directly under your shoulders and body forming a straight line.
execution_steps: Drive your right knee toward your chest quickly.
As you return the right foot to the start, simultaneously drive the left knee toward your chest.
Alternate rapidly as if running in a plank position.
common_mistakes: Bouncing the hips up and down
Looking back at the feet instead of slightly forward
breathing_pattern: Breathe rapidly and continuously.

exercise_setup: Sit on a bench with back support inside a rack. Grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width.
execution_steps: Unrack the bar and hold it at upper chest/collarbone level.
Press the bar straight up overhead until your arms are fully locked out.
Slowly lower the bar back to the upper chest under control.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back excessively to turn it into an incline press
Bouncing the bar off the chest
cues: Keep lower back flat against the pad
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

contraindications: Poor shoulder/wrist mobility (to hold bar behind)
exercise_setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, with a barbell on the floor behind your legs. Squat down and grip the bar behind you with an overhand grip.
execution_steps: Keep your chest up and back flat.
Drive through your heels to stand up, dragging the barbell up the back of your calves and thighs.
Squeeze your glutes and quads at the top, then lower the bar back to the floor.
common_mistakes: Letting the bar swing away from the legs
Hips shooting up before the chest
cues: Drag the bar up your legs
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace before lifting, exhale at the top.

exercise_setup: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley. Stand close to the machine, holding the bar with an overhand grip.
execution_steps: Keep your arms straight and elevate your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
The cable provides constant tension throughout the movement, pulling slightly forward as well as down.
Squeeze the traps hard at the top, then lower slowly.
breathing_pattern: Exhale while shrugging, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand tall. Take two flat weight plates (e.g., two 10lb or 25lb plates with smooth sides out) in one or both hands.
execution_steps: Pinch the plates together using only your fingertips and thumb (do not hook your fingers through the holes).
Hold the plates by your sides for as long as possible.
Keep your chest up and shoulders pulled back.
common_mistakes: Resting the plates against the leg to cheat
Hooking fingers in the plate holes
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously.

exercise_setup: Sit on the floor with your legs straight out in front of you in a V-shape. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
execution_steps: Keep your torso completely upright by intensely bracing your core and hip flexors.
Press the dumbbells straight up overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Lower them under control. If your core weakens, you will fall backward.
common_mistakes: Pressing the dumbbells forward instead of straight up
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pressing, inhale while lowering.
regressions: Seated Dumbbell Press (on bench with back support)

contraindications: Shoulder pain (due to fixed bar path)
exercise_setup: Center a flat bench under the Smith machine bar. Lie back so the bar aligns with your mid-chest. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
execution_steps: Unrack the bar by rotating it.
Lower the bar slowly to your chest. The machine guides the path.
Press the bar forcefully back up to full extension.
common_mistakes: Positioning the bench too far forward or backward (causing an unnatural pressing angle)
Bouncing the bar off the chest
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

contraindications: Shoulder impingement (due to fixed bar path)
exercise_setup: Place a bench with back support under the Smith machine. Align the bench so the bar lowers just in front of your face. Grip the bar wider than shoulder-width.
execution_steps: Unrack the bar.
Lower the bar to chin or upper chest level.
Press the bar straight up until your arms are fully extended.
common_mistakes: Setting the bench too far back (strains the rotator cuff)
Arching the back off the pad
cues: Bar path just clears the nose
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Set a low cable pulley. Stand sideways to the machine and grab the handle with your outside hand. The cable runs across the front of your body.
execution_steps: Keeping a slight bend in your elbow, raise the handle out to the side until it reaches shoulder height.
Squeeze the side delt.
Slowly lower it back down. The cable provides constant tension unlike a dumbbell.
common_mistakes: Leaning aggressively away from the machine to cheat
breathing_pattern: Exhale while raising, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Set a cable pulley to a low or mid height. Turn away from the machine, grab the handle with one hand, and bring it behind your head.
execution_steps: Adopt a staggered stance.
Keeping your elbow pointing forward and stationary, extend your arm straight up and forward.
Squeeze the triceps, then slowly return to a deep stretch behind the head.
common_mistakes: Flaring the elbow out to the side
Moving the upper arm (turning it into a press)
breathing_pattern: Exhale while extending, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Sit in the machine and adjust the seat so your armpits rest comfortably over the top of the pad. Grip the handles.
execution_steps: Curl the handles upward toward your shoulders, squeezing the biceps at the peak.
Slowly lower the handles back down until your arms are fully extended.
Do not hyperextend the elbows at the bottom.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to pull the weight
Not fully extending at the bottom
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand holding dumbbells by your sides. Brace your core.
execution_steps: Take a large step forward with one leg and lower your hips until both knees are bent at 90-degree angles.
Drive through the heel of the front foot to push yourself up and immediately step forward with the opposite leg into the next lunge.
Continue walking forward continuously.
common_mistakes: Taking steps that are too short (stresses the front knee)
breathing_pattern: Inhale as you step and drop, exhale as you drive up.

exercise_setup: Attach a rope to a low cable pulley. Stand facing the machine and grip the rope with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
execution_steps: Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
Curl the rope up toward your shoulders, pulling the ends of the rope slightly apart at the top.
Squeeze the forearms and biceps, then slowly lower the rope back to a full extension.
cues: Spread the rope at the top
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Attach a harness or straps to a sled. Face away from the sled. If using straps, hold them over your shoulders or at your sides.
execution_steps: Lean your body forward aggressively, keeping tension on the straps.
Drive your legs into the ground, taking powerful steps forward to drag the sled behind you.
Keep your core braced and spine neutral.
common_mistakes: Standing too upright and losing leverage
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously and heavily.

exercise_setup: Attach a rope to a high cable pulley. Kneel on a mat facing the machine, holding the rope behind your neck.
execution_steps: Keeping your hips relatively stationary, contract your abs to curl your torso downward.
Bring your elbows toward your knees, rounding your upper back.
Slowly return to the starting position without letting the weight stack rest.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms instead of the abs
Flexing at the hips instead of the spine
Arching the lower back on the return
breathing_pattern: Exhale while crunching down, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Lie on your back on the floor with knees bent. Hold a dumbbell in each hand above your chest.
execution_steps: Lower the dumbbells under control until your upper arms rest completely on the floor.
Pause for a split second to kill the momentum.
Press the dumbbells explosively back to lockout.
common_mistakes: Bouncing the triceps off the floor
Lifting the hips off the floor to cheat
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Clean a kettlebell into the rack position on one side. Stand tall, brace your core, and squeeze your glutes.
execution_steps: Press the kettlebell straight up overhead, allowing your arm to rotate naturally so your palm faces forward at the top.
Lock out the elbow with your bicep close to your ear.
Actively pull the kettlebell back down to the rack position.
breathing_pattern: Inhale before pressing, exhale at lockout.

exercise_setup: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor. Roll a padded barbell over your hips.
execution_steps: Hold the bar to keep it stable.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes extremely hard at the top.
Lower under control.
common_mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back instead of locking out the hips
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while thrusting up.

exercise_setup: Sit facing the machine pad. Adjust the seat so the handles are at shoulder level. Grab the handles with a neutral or pronated grip.
execution_steps: Keep a slight bend in your elbows and pull the handles backward in an arc.
Squeeze your rear delts and upper back at the end of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position without letting the weight stack crash.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the triceps instead of the rear delts
cues: Squeeze the back of the shoulder
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling back, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Set a barbell on pins in a rack just below glute level. Stand facing away from the bar and grab it with an overhand grip.
execution_steps: Keep your arms straight and your chest proud.
Shrug your shoulders up and slightly back toward your ears.
Hold the squeeze at the top, then lower the bar to a full stretch.
breathing_pattern: Exhale while shrugging, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand on one leg, holding a dumbbell in the hand opposite to the planted leg (or in both hands). Keep a soft bend in the planted knee.
execution_steps: Hinge at the hips, extending your free leg straight back behind you for balance.
Lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor, feeling a deep stretch in the planted hamstring.
Drive your hips forward to stand back up.
common_mistakes: Bending the planted knee too much
Opening the hips to the side instead of keeping them square
cues: Push the back heel to the wall
breathing_pattern: Inhale while hinging down, exhale while standing up.

exercise_setup: Strap a weight belt around your waist and attach plates. Grab the pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
execution_steps: From a dead hang, pull your chest up toward the bar by driving your elbows down.
Clear the bar with your chin.
Lower yourself under control back to a full dead hang.
common_mistakes: Not fully extending the arms at the bottom
Reaching with the chin instead of pulling the chest up
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Strap a weight belt around your waist. Mount the parallel bars and lock out your arms.
execution_steps: Keep your torso relatively upright to target the triceps.
Lower your body by bending your elbows to 90 degrees.
Press forcefully back up to full lockout.
common_mistakes: Going too deep and over-stretching the shoulder capsule
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Sit in the leg press machine. Place one foot in the middle of the sled and let the other leg rest safely out of the way.
execution_steps: Unrack the sled.
Lower the sled by bending your knee and hip as deep as comfortable without rounding your lower back.
Drive through your entire foot to push the sled back up.
common_mistakes: Letting the working knee cave inward
Lifting the heel off the sled
Twisting the hips in the seat
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Set a low cable pulley. Stand next to the machine, holding the vertical beam with your inside hand. Grab the cable handle with your outside hand.
execution_steps: Lean your body away from the machine until your inside arm is fully extended. Keep your feet planted.
Raise the cable handle out to the side until it is parallel to the floor.
Slowly lower it back down. The lean increases the range of motion and alters the resistance profile.
breathing_pattern: Exhale while raising, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Set a cable pulley to the bottom. Grab the handle and stand facing away from the machine, stepping forward to create tension.
execution_steps: Let your arm be pulled slightly behind your body, stretching the bicep.
Keeping your elbow stationary behind your torso, curl the handle forward and up.
Squeeze the bicep, then slowly return to the stretched position.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbow swing forward during the curl
Not letting the arm go behind the body
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit at the lat pulldown machine. Grab the bar with a supinated (underhand) grip, roughly shoulder-width apart.
execution_steps: Keep your chest up and lean back slightly.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back.
Squeeze your lats and biceps, then slowly let the bar return to a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Pulling the bar down to the stomach
Rounding the shoulders forward at the bottom
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Sit at the lat pulldown machine. Grab the bar with a pronated (overhand) grip, wider than shoulder-width.
execution_steps: Keep your chest up.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest by driving your elbows straight down toward your sides.
Squeeze your lats, then slowly let the bar return to a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Pulling the bar behind the neck (dangerous for rotator cuff)
Pulling with the arms instead of the back
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Step inside a loaded trap bar. Use relatively light weight (20-30% of 1RM). Hinge down and grip the handles.
execution_steps: Drop your hips and lift your chest.
Explosively drive through the floor to jump straight up into the air as high as possible while holding the bar.
Absorb the landing by bending your knees and hips, resetting completely before the next jump.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back during the jump or landing
breathing_pattern: Inhale before jumping, exhale in the air.

exercise_setup: Stand holding a pair of dumbbells. Clean them up so they rest vertically on the front of your shoulders, elbows pointing forward.
execution_steps: Keep your chest tall and core braced.
Sit your hips back and down to squat as deep as possible.
Drive through your feet to return to a standing position.
common_mistakes: Dropping the elbows and rounding the upper back
breathing_pattern: Inhale while descending, exhale while ascending.

exercise_setup: Set a cable pulley to chest height. Stand sideways to the machine, grab the handle with both hands, and step out to create tension.
execution_steps: Keep your arms straight and horizontal.
Rotate your torso to pull the handle across your body.
Pivot your back foot slightly. Slowly return to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms instead of rotating the core
breathing_pattern: Exhale while twisting, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Secure your legs on a decline bench. Lie back holding dumbbells directly above your lower chest with a neutral grip.
execution_steps: With a slight bend in your elbows, slowly lower the dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc.
Stop when you feel a stretch in your lower chest.
Squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbells back together in a hugging motion.
common_mistakes: Pressing the weight instead of flying
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while bringing them together.

exercise_setup: Place a barbell across your upper back. Stand facing a sturdy box or bench.
execution_steps: Place one foot entirely on the box.
Drive through the heel of the elevated foot to step up until the leg is fully straight.
Slowly and carefully step back down to the floor, controlling the descent.
common_mistakes: Pushing off the floor with the back leg instead of pulling with the front leg
Letting the front knee cave inward
Losing balance due to the barbell
breathing_pattern: Exhale while stepping up, inhale while stepping down.

exercise_setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Clean a dumbbell to shoulder height on one side.
execution_steps: Perform a quick, shallow dip by bending your knees slightly.
Explosively drive your legs to launch the dumbbell upward.
Finish pressing the dumbbell overhead until your arm is locked out. The core must work overtime to prevent torso rotation.
common_mistakes: Pressing early before the leg drive
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace before the dip, exhale at lockout.

exercise_setup: Stand facing the landmine with feet shoulder-width apart. Hold the end of the barbell with both hands, arms extended in front of your chest.
execution_steps: Keeping your arms relatively straight, pivot your feet and rotate your torso to swing the barbell down to one side.
Stop before it touches your hip.
Explosively contract your core to swing the barbell back up and over to the opposite side.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows instead of using the core
Not pivoting the feet (strains the knees)
breathing_pattern: Exhale aggressively as you swing up, inhale as you lower.

exercise_setup: Get into a standard push-up position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your core tightly braced.
execution_steps: As you lower your chest toward the floor, lift your right foot off the ground and bring your right knee out and up to touch your right elbow.
Push back up to the starting position while simultaneously returning your leg.
Repeat on the other side.
common_mistakes: Losing balance and twisting the torso too much
cues: Knee to elbow at the bottom
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering and bringing the knee up, exhale while pressing back.

exercise_setup: Start in a downward dog position (hips high in the air, forming an inverted V).
execution_steps: Swoop your body down by bending your elbows, bringing your head and chest close to the floor as if sliding under a low fence.
Push your chest up and forward, extending your arms and arching your back (upward dog position).
Push your hips straight back up to the starting inverted V position (do not swoop backward).
common_mistakes: Swooping backward instead of just pushing the hips up (turns it into a Dive Bomber)
Letting the lower back sag without core control
breathing_pattern: Inhale as you swoop down and up, exhale as you push the hips back.
progressions: Dive Bomber Push-Up (swoop backward to return)

exercise_setup: Grip a barbell with a supinated (underhand) grip at shoulder-width. Hinge at the hips until your torso is at a 45 to 60-degree angle (slightly more upright than a standard row).
execution_steps: Pull the barbell into your lower stomach or waistline.
Keep your elbows tucked tight against your body.
Squeeze your lats and biceps, then lower the bar under control.
common_mistakes: Pulling the bar too high (to the chest) which strains the wrists
breathing_pattern: Exhale while rowing, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Set a low cable pulley. Stand close to the machine. Grab the vertical pole with your non-working hand and lean away from the machine.
execution_steps: The cable should run behind your legs.
Keeping a slight bend in your working elbow, raise the handle out to the side until your arm is parallel to the floor.
Slowly lower it back down, letting the cable pull your arm slightly behind your body for a maximum stretch.
common_mistakes: Pulling the cable in front of the legs instead of behind
breathing_pattern: Exhale while raising, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Lie on a flat bench holding two dumbbells. Press them together so they are touching side-by-side over your chest.
execution_steps: Squeeze the dumbbells together as hard as you can (isometric contraction of the chest).
Maintaining this outward pressure, lower the dumbbells to your mid-chest.
Press them back up to full lockout, never letting them separate.
common_mistakes: Not actively squeezing them together (which defeats the purpose)
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Secure your legs on a decline bench. Hold an EZ-bar with a narrow overhand grip, arms extended straight up over your lower chest.
execution_steps: Angle your arms slightly backward (towards your head).
Bend your elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead or slightly behind your head.
Feel the deep stretch in the triceps (enhanced by the decline angle), then press back up.
common_mistakes: Moving the upper arms too much (turning it into a pullover)
Lowering the bar to the nose/mouth
cues: Lock the upper arms in place
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while extending.

exercise_setup: Set the Smith machine bar at mid-thigh level. Stand facing the bar and grab it with an overhand grip, shoulder-width apart.
execution_steps: Unrack the bar.
Keeping your arms perfectly straight, elevate your shoulders as high as possible toward your ears.
Squeeze the traps at the top, then slowly lower the bar back to a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows to lift the weight
breathing_pattern: Exhale while shrugging, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Bridge your hips up so your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
execution_steps: Keeping your hips elevated and perfectly level, lift your right foot off the floor and drive your right knee toward your chest.
Place the right foot back down.
Without letting your hips sag, lift your left foot and drive the left knee toward your chest. Alternate legs.
common_mistakes: Hips twisting side to side when lifting a leg
cues: Push through the heel of the planted foot
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously and rhythmically.
progressions: Weighted Glute Bridge March (sandbag on hips)

exercise_setup: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, stepping on one end of a large looped resistance band. Loop the other end over the back of your neck.
execution_steps: Keep your knees slightly bent and your back perfectly flat.
Hinge at the hips, pushing your glutes backward until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
Drive your hips forward against the band resistance to stand back up, squeezing your glutes.
common_mistakes: Bending the knees into a squat
Looking straight up and straining the neck
cues: Squeeze the glutes at the top
breathing_pattern: Inhale while hinging, exhale while standing up.

exercise_setup: Stand on a very low box or weight plate. The working foot should have the heel elevated (using a wedge or plate). The non-working leg hangs off the side or front.
execution_steps: Keeping your torso completely upright, bend the working knee to let the non-working heel touch the floor gently.
Ensure the working knee tracks far forward over the toes.
Push through the working leg to straighten the knee back up.
common_mistakes: Pushing off the floor with the non-working foot
breathing_pattern: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you step up.
progressions: Increase the height of the step

exercise_setup: Set a cable pulley to a high or low position (depending on preference). If low, bend over and rest your triceps against your inner thigh. If high, stand and curl toward your ear.
execution_steps: Keeping your upper arm completely stationary, curl the handle toward your shoulder/head.
Squeeze the bicep forcefully at the peak of the contraction.
Slowly let the cable pull your arm back to full extension.
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling, inhale while extending.

exercise_setup: Attach a wide bar to a high cable pulley. Stand facing the machine, step back to create tension, and hinge your torso slightly forward.
execution_steps: Keep your arms straight with a very slight, locked bend in the elbows.
Push the bar down in a wide arc until it touches your thighs.
Squeeze your lats and core, then slowly let the bar return upward until you feel a deep stretch in the lats.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows (turning it into a triceps pushdown)
cues: Sweep the bar to your pockets
Feel the stretch at the top
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pushing down, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Lie on your side on a mat. Cross your top leg over your bottom leg, planting the top foot flat on the floor in front of you. Keep the bottom leg straight.
execution_steps: Flex your bottom foot (toes pointing forward).
Lift the straight bottom leg upward toward the ceiling, engaging the inner thigh.
Hold for a second at the top, then slowly lower back down without resting it completely.
breathing_pattern: Exhale while lifting, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit on the edge of a bench with a mini resistance band looped just above your knees. Feet flat on the floor, close together.
execution_steps: Sit up tall and brace your core.
Drive your knees outward against the band as far as possible.
Squeeze the side of your glutes hard at the widest point, then slowly return to the center under control.
common_mistakes: Letting the band snap the knees back together rapidly
Rolling onto the outside of the feet too much
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pushing out, inhale while returning.
progressions: Leaning Forward/Backward to hit different glute fibers

exercise_setup: Stand holding a medicine ball with both hands. Feet shoulder-width apart.
execution_steps: Squat slightly and twist to bring the ball down to the outside of your right knee.
In one fluid motion, stand up, pivot your right foot, and swing the ball diagonally upward across your body so it ends high above your left shoulder.
Control the ball back down to the right knee.
common_mistakes: Moving only the arms instead of rotating the torso
Arching the lower back at the top
breathing_pattern: Exhale aggressively as you chop upward, inhale as you lower.

exercise_setup: Sit on the floor. Plant your hands behind you (fingers pointing away or to the sides) and bend your knees to plant your feet flat.
execution_steps: Push your hips up off the floor so you are supported only by your hands and feet (tabletop position).
Walk forward by stepping with your right hand and left foot, then left hand and right foot.
Keep your hips elevated throughout the crawl.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips sag to the floor
Looking straight up and straining the neck
Taking steps that are too large
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously.

exercise_setup: Kneel on a mat with your hands on the handles of an ab wheel directly under your shoulders.
execution_steps: Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and slowly roll the wheel forward.
Go as far as you can while maintaining a perfectly straight, slightly hollowed back.
Once fully extended, use your core and lats to pull the wheel back to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Hinging at the hips (sticking the butt out) instead of rolling the body out as one unit
Letting the lower back sag (causes severe pain)
breathing_pattern: Inhale while rolling out, exhale while pulling back.

primary_muscles: Neck Extensors (Splenius Capitis, Erector Spinae Cervicis)
contraindications: Any history of neck pain, cervical disc herniation, or spine issues
exercise_setup: Lie on your back on a soft mat. Bend your knees and plant your feet. Place your hands by your ears (fingers pointing to toes).
execution_steps: Push your hips up into a glute bridge while simultaneously pushing through your hands and head to arch your back.
Roll back onto the crown of your head.
Remove your hands (only if advanced) and hold the bridge, supporting your weight with your legs and neck.
common_mistakes: Putting all the weight on the neck without using the legs
Attempting this without prior neck conditioning
cues: Keep hands on the floor for safety if unsure
breathing_pattern: Breathe shallowly into the braced core.

exercise_setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Lift one leg off the ground, straightening it or pulling the knee toward your chest.
execution_steps: Drive through the heel of the planted foot to lift your hips off the ground.
Your body should form a straight line from the planted knee to your shoulders.
Squeeze the glute of the working leg, then lower your hips back down under control.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back instead of extending the hip
Hips twisting toward the unsupported side
breathing_pattern: Exhale while thrusting up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Hold one end of a resistance band in each hand and loop it securely across your upper back/shoulders. Get into a standard push-up position.
execution_steps: Lower your chest toward the floor.
Press back up explosively. The band will stretch and increase the resistance significantly at the top of the movement (accommodating resistance).
Lock out the elbows fully.
common_mistakes: Letting the band snap your body down uncontrollably
Hips sagging to compensate for the band tension
Not locking out at the top
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale forcefully while pressing.

exercise_setup: Adjust the seat so the thigh pads lock your legs in firmly. Grab the handles (perform unilaterally for better focus, or bilaterally).
execution_steps: Pull the handle down and slightly back, driving your elbow toward your hip.
Squeeze your lat hard at the bottom of the movement.
Control the weight back up until your arm is fully extended and you feel a deep stretch.
common_mistakes: Using excessive body english to swing the weight down
Pulling with the biceps instead of the back
Not reaching a full stretch at the top
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling down, inhale while returning.

primary_muscles: Quadriceps (Rectus Femoris, Vastus Lateralis, Vastus Medialis, Vastus Intermedius)
exercise_setup: Sit in the leg extension machine. Adjust the pad so it rests on your lower shin. Rest one leg out of the way or lightly on the pad without pushing.
execution_steps: Using only one leg, extend your knee to lift the pad until your leg is fully straight.
Squeeze your quad forcefully at the peak contraction.
Slowly lower the pad back down under control.
common_mistakes: Swinging the leg to use momentum
Lifting the hip off the seat
breathing_pattern: Exhale while extending, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Set a bench to a 30-45 degree incline. Lie back holding a dumbbell with both hands (diamond grip) straight up over your chest.
execution_steps: Keeping a slight, fixed bend in your elbows, slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head.
The incline angle alters the resistance profile, putting maximum stretch on the lats earlier in the movement compared to a flat bench.
Pull the dumbbell back over your chest.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows (turning it into a triceps extension)
Arching the lower back excessively off the pad
breathing_pattern: Inhale deeply while lowering, exhale while pulling back.

exercise_setup: Set up a barbell back squat and securely attach resistance bands from the bottom of the rack (or heavy dumbbells on the floor) to the ends of the barbell.
execution_steps: Unrack the bar and step back.
As you squat down, the bands provide less resistance.
As you drive up, you must explode through the movement because the bands stretch and the resistance gets continuously heavier toward the top.
common_mistakes: Squatting slowly on the way up
Letting the bands pull you out of position
Not using enough base weight (the bar might whip)
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace before descending, exhale forcefully while standing up.

exercise_setup: Set the cable pulleys to a high position. Stand in the center, grab the handles, and step forward into a staggered stance to create tension.
execution_steps: Lean your torso slightly forward.
Press the handles downward and forward in a decline path, extending your elbows.
Squeeze your lower chest, then slowly let your arms return to the starting stretched position.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a fly instead of a press (not bending elbows enough)
Using body momentum to throw the weight
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pressing, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Hold the TRX handles with arms slightly bent. Stand on one leg and extend the other leg straight out in front of you.
execution_steps: Lower your body into a single-leg squat, using the TRX straps for balance and slight assistance.
Go as deep as your mobility allows (ideally hamstrings to calves).
Drive through the foot of the planted leg and use your arms to help pull yourself back to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Relying too much on the arms to pull up
Letting the planted heel lift off the ground
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while standing up.

exercise_setup: Lie flat on a bench (either normally or perpendicular across it). Hold a barbell over your chest with a shoulder-width or slightly narrower overhand grip.
execution_steps: Keep a slight, locked bend in your elbows.
Slowly lower the barbell in an arc behind your head until you feel a deep stretch in your lats and ribcage.
Pull the barbell back over your chest in the same arc.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows into a skull crusher
Dropping the bar too low and straining the shoulder joint
Arching the back completely off the bench
breathing_pattern: Inhale deeply while lowering, exhale while pulling back.

exercise_setup: Sit upright on a flat bench holding dumbbells by your sides with a neutral grip.
execution_steps: Keep your arms straight and your chest proud.
Elevate your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as possible.
Hold the peak contraction for a second, then lower the dumbbells slowly back to a full stretch. Sitting prevents using leg drive to cheat.
breathing_pattern: Exhale while shrugging up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width. Hinge down and grip the kettlebell with one hand.
execution_steps: Hike the kettlebell back between your legs.
Explosively drive your hips forward to swing the bell up to chest height.
Keep your core braced tightly to prevent your torso from twisting as the asymmetrical load pulls on you.
Let the bell drop naturally and hinge at the hips to absorb the force.
common_mistakes: Lifting the bell with the shoulder
Letting the torso twist with the bell
breathing_pattern: Inhale as the bell drops, exhale sharply on the hip snap.

exercise_setup: Set two low cable pulleys close together. Stand straddling the cables facing away from the machine. Grab the left handle with your left hand and right handle with your right hand (the cables come from between your legs).
execution_steps: Lean slightly forward.
Raise the handles out to the sides and slightly forward until they reach shoulder height.
Slowly lower them back down. This setup changes the angle of pull to load the lengthened position of the lateral delt intensely.
breathing_pattern: Exhale while raising, inhale while lowering.
regressions: Standard Cable Lateral Raise (from the sides)

exercise_setup: Start in a high plank position with your hands on the floor and your shins resting on a Swiss ball.
execution_steps: Keeping your legs completely straight, contract your abs and pull the ball toward your chest, raising your hips high into the air (forming an inverted V or pike position).
Pause briefly at the top.
Slowly control the ball back to the starting plank position.
common_mistakes: Bending the knees (turning it into a tuck)
Letting the hips sag past the straight plank position on the return
breathing_pattern: Exhale while piking up, inhale while returning to plank.

exercise_setup: Start in a high plank position with your hands on the floor and your shins resting on a Swiss ball.
execution_steps: Contract your abs and bend your knees to pull the ball straight in toward your chest.
Squeeze the abs hard.
Slowly extend your legs back out to the starting plank position, maintaining a tight core so the hips don't sag.
common_mistakes: Dropping the hips below the plank level
Using momentum instead of controlled contraction
Looking down at the ball instead of slightly forward
cues: Body like a board in the start position
breathing_pattern: Exhale while tucking knees, inhale while extending.

exercise_setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding dumbbells by your sides. Hinge slightly at the hips and bend the knees to lower the weights.
execution_steps: Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles while simultaneously shrugging your shoulders.
Pull the dumbbells straight up close to your body.
Quickly drop under the weights, rotating your elbows forward to catch the dumbbells on the front of your shoulders in a quarter-squat position.
Stand up tall to finish.
common_mistakes: Reverse curling the weight instead of using hip power
Swinging the dumbbells out in a wide arc
Not dropping under to catch the weight
breathing_pattern: Inhale before the pull, exhale upon standing.

exercise_setup: Loop a heavy resistance band around a sturdy rig near the floor. Face away from the rig, straddle the band, and hold the loop between your legs.
execution_steps: Walk forward to create tension.
Hinge at the hips, letting the band pull your hands backward between your legs while you push your glutes back.
Keep a flat back and a slight knee bend.
Drive your hips forward against the band to stand up, squeezing the glutes hard at lockout.
common_mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back at the top
breathing_pattern: Inhale while hinging back, exhale while driving forward.

exercise_setup: Step into the machine, locking your ankles under the front pads and resting your calves against the rear pad.
execution_steps: Keeping your body in a straight line from your knees to your head, lean backward, allowing your knees to bend.
Go as deep as you comfortably can, feeling a massive stretch in the quads.
Use your quads to pull yourself back to the upright starting position.
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips (sitting down) instead of leaning back
cues: Straight line from knee to head
breathing_pattern: Inhale while leaning back, exhale while returning.
progressions: Weighted Machine Sissy Squat (holding a plate)

exercise_setup: Attach a D-handle to a low pulley. Hinge forward or kneel so your torso is supported. Rest the triceps of the working arm against the inside of your thigh (if standing/bending) or let it hang straight down.
execution_steps: Keeping the upper arm completely still, curl the handle toward your shoulder.
Squeeze the bicep hard at the peak contraction.
Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Not fully extending at the bottom
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling, inhale while extending.

exercise_setup: Set a flat bench under the Smith machine. Grip the bar with a close grip (shoulder-width or slightly narrower).
execution_steps: Unrack the bar. Lower it straight down toward your neck/upper chest area.
As you lower it, allow your elbows to track forward toward your hips (a hybrid of a skull crusher and close-grip bench).
Once the forearms touch the biceps, press the bar back up to full lockout.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a pure bench press by dropping the elbows down instead of forward
Turning it into a pure skull crusher
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Attach a rope to a high pulley. Stand facing away from the machine with the rope held securely behind your neck. Hinge slightly at the hips to start.
execution_steps: Keep your hips locked in position.
Contract your abs to curl your torso downward, bringing your chest toward your pelvis.
Slowly return to the starting position without letting the weight stack pull you into hyperextension.
common_mistakes: Hinging at the hips (like a good morning) instead of flexing the spine
Leaning back too far at the top
breathing_pattern: Exhale while crunching, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Step inside a trap bar loaded with 20-30% of your 1RM. Grip the handles and drop your hips.
execution_steps: Explosively drive through the floor to jump straight up, holding the bar.
Aim for maximum height.
Absorb the landing by landing softly with bent knees and hips, returning the bar to the floor.
Reset completely before the next jump.
common_mistakes: Using weight that is too heavy to actually jump
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace before jumping, exhale mid-air.

exercise_setup: Sit on the floor with legs straight out in a V-shape. Clean a kettlebell into the rack position on one side.
execution_steps: Keeping your torso completely upright, press the kettlebell straight overhead.
Lock out your elbow with your bicep close to your ear.
Actively pull the weight back down to the rack position.
common_mistakes: Not locking out at the top
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pressing, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Unrack the barbell on your back (or in the front rack for a front Sots press). Descend into a deep, rock-bottom squat.
execution_steps: Hold the deep squat position.
Press the barbell overhead to a full lockout.
Lower the bar back to your shoulders while remaining in the deep squat.
common_mistakes: Not achieving full lockout due to mobility restrictions
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pressing, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand under the Smith machine bar, resting it on your upper back. Unrack the bar.
execution_steps: Take a step backward with one foot and lower your hips until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
The back knee should hover just above the ground.
Drive through the front heel to return to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Stepping too far back or not far enough
Letting the front knee collapse inward
breathing_pattern: Inhale while stepping back, exhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Attach straps to a sled. Stand sideways to the sled, holding the straps with both hands at your hips.
execution_steps: Lean slightly away from the sled.
Take deliberate side-steps, crossing the trailing leg in front of or behind the lead leg, dragging the sled laterally.
