Keep your toes pointing relatively straight ahead.
common_mistakes: Rotating the hips to face the sled
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously.

exercise_setup: Sit on the edge of a bench. Place your hands next to your hips, gripping the edge. Walk your feet out so your hips slide off the bench (legs straight or knees bent).
execution_steps: Lower your body by bending your elbows until they reach roughly 90 degrees.
Keep your back close to the bench.
Push through your palms to return to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips drift far away from the bench (strains the shoulders)
cues: Keep back close to the bench
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Lie flat on a bench holding a dumbbell vertically by one end. Press it straight over your chest.
execution_steps: Keep your elbows pointing straight up, let the dumbbell drop behind your head by bending your elbows (like a skull crusher).
Once the elbows are bent past 90 degrees, let your shoulders flex slightly to drop the dumbbell even lower for a massive stretch.
Reverse the motion, using the triceps to press back up.
common_mistakes: Turning it entirely into a lat pullover
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while extending.

exercise_setup: Stand with your front foot on a 2-4 inch weight plate or low box. Hold dumbbells by your sides.
execution_steps: Step backward off the plate with one foot.
Lower your hips until your back knee almost touches the floor, getting a deeper stretch in the front leg due to the elevation.
Drive through the front heel to return to the plate.
common_mistakes: Pushing off the back foot too much
breathing_pattern: Inhale while stepping back, exhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Stand on a box (6-12 inches). Stand on one leg near the edge.
execution_steps: Slowly bend your standing knee to lower your other foot toward the floor.
Take 3-5 seconds to control the descent.
Tap the heel lightly, then use both legs (or hold a rig) to stand back up (focus is on the slow lowering phase).
common_mistakes: Reaching for the floor with the toes instead of bending the knee
breathing_pattern: Breathe naturally during the slow descent.

exercise_setup: Place heel wedges or small plates under your heels. Step inside the trap bar. Hinge down to grip the handles.
execution_steps: Because of the heel elevation, your knees will track further forward, turning the movement into a squat-bias.
Keep your chest up and drive through your feet to stand tall.
Control the weight back to the floor.
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace before lifting, exhale at the top.

exercise_setup: Hold a barbell with an overhand grip. Stagger your feet: one foot flat (working leg), the other foot stepped slightly back resting only on the toes (kickstand).
execution_steps: Keep 80% of your weight on the front foot.
Hinge at the hips, pushing them back to lower the barbell along your front leg.
Feel the stretch in the front hamstring, then drive the hips forward to stand back up.
common_mistakes: Shifting weight to the back foot
Bending the front knee too much
breathing_pattern: Inhale while hinging, exhale while standing.

exercise_setup: Set a cable pulley to chest height. Stand sideways to the machine, holding the handle with both hands against your chest. Step out to create tension.
execution_steps: Brace your core tightly.
Press the handle straight out in front of you. The cable will try to violently twist your torso toward the machine.
Resist the rotation, hold for 2-3 seconds at full extension, and bring it back to your chest.
cues: Lock the hips and shoulders square
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pressing out, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Loop a resistance band around a rig at chest height. Stand sideways to the rig, holding the band with both hands at your chest. Step out to create tension.
execution_steps: Brace your core.
Press the band straight out in front of you. The resistance increases as you press.
Hold for 2-3 seconds, fighting the rotation, then return to the chest.
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pressing out, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Hang from a pull-up bar or support yourself on a Captain's chair.
execution_steps: Contract your abs to lift your knees up toward your chest.
Slightly curl your pelvis upward at the top of the movement to fully engage the lower abs.
Slowly lower your legs back down without swinging.
common_mistakes: Using momentum to swing the legs
Only using hip flexors (not curling the pelvis)
breathing_pattern: Exhale while raising knees, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand holding an ab wheel. Bend at the hips to place the wheel on the floor in front of your feet.
execution_steps: Keeping your legs straight and core aggressively braced, roll the wheel forward.
Roll out as far as possible until your body is nearly parallel to the floor.
Use your core and lats to pull the wheel back to your feet.
common_mistakes: Letting the lower back sag (causes immediate pain)
breathing_pattern: Inhale while rolling out, exhale while pulling back.

exercise_setup: Have a partner place a weight plate on your mid/upper back, or carefully slide it on yourself. Get into a forearm plank position.
execution_steps: Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and push the floor away with your elbows.
Keep your body in a perfectly straight line from head to heels.
Hold the position for time, resisting the extra weight pushing you down.
common_mistakes: Letting the shoulder blades wing together
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously and shallowly.

exercise_setup: Grip a kettlebell by the handle and clean it so the heavy bell portion is pointing straight up to the ceiling (bottoms-up). Keep your elbow bent at 90 degrees.
execution_steps: Crush the handle to keep the bell balanced.
Walk forward slowly and deliberately, keeping your posture perfect and core braced.
If the bell starts to fall, safely guide it down.
common_mistakes: Taking your eyes off the bell
breathing_pattern: Breathe rhythmically.

exercise_setup: Grab one TRX handle. Lean back until your arm is straight, feet planted. Place your free hand on your hip or chest.
execution_steps: Keep your body in a straight line and resist the urge to twist your torso.
Pull your chest up toward the handle by driving your elbow back.
Slowly lower back down under control.
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso to cheat the movement
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand facing away from the TRX anchor. Hold the handles with straight arms at chest height, leaning forward slightly on your toes.
execution_steps: Keeping your body completely rigid, slowly raise your arms overhead, letting your body fall forward.
Go as far as you can control without your lower back arching.
Use your core and lats to pull your arms back down, returning to the start.
breathing_pattern: Inhale as you fall forward, exhale as you return.

exercise_setup: Stand with your back, head, and glutes against a wall. Raise your arms to 90 degrees (goalpost position) with your elbows and back of hands touching the wall.
execution_steps: Slowly slide your arms up the wall, trying to straighten them overhead without letting your elbows or hands lose contact with the wall.
Do not let your lower back arch off the wall.
Slide back down to the start.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back to compensate for poor shoulder mobility
breathing_pattern: Breathe continuously.

exercise_setup: Get into a Copenhagen Plank position (top foot on a bench, bottom elbow on the floor, hips elevated).
execution_steps: Slowly lower your hips toward the floor until they lightly tap the ground.
Powerfully squeeze the inner thigh of the top leg to lift your hips back up to a perfectly straight line.
Keep your body facing forward; don't rotate.
common_mistakes: Using the bottom leg to push off the floor
breathing_pattern: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you lift.

exercise_setup: Lie face down on the Reverse Hyper machine with your hips at the edge of the pad. Secure your ankles in the straps.
execution_steps: Keeping your legs relatively straight, swing your legs upward until they are in line with your torso.
Squeeze your glutes and lower back at the top.
Control the weight back down, allowing your lower back to stretch and decompress.
common_mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back at the top
breathing_pattern: Exhale while lifting, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit on the GHD machine, locking your feet securely. Your glutes should be off the pad, supported only by your hamstrings/calves.
execution_steps: Lean back, extending your spine over the edge of the pad until your hands touch the floor (or go as far as mobility allows).
Aggressively contract your abs and fire your quads to pull your torso back up to the seated position.
Touch the foot pads to complete the rep.
common_mistakes: Not using the quads to initiate the upward pull
Doing high reps without prior conditioning
cues: Use the legs to assist the core
breathing_pattern: Inhale as you fall back, exhale powerfully as you sit up.

exercise_setup: Step under the shoulder pads of the machine. Place the balls of your feet on the edge of the block. Unrack the weight.
execution_steps: Lower your heels as far down as possible to deeply stretch the calves.
Drive through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
Squeeze the calves hard at the peak.
breathing_pattern: Exhale while raising, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit in the machine and place the balls of your feet on the platform. Adjust the knee pads so they rest comfortably on your lower thighs. Unrack the lever.
execution_steps: Lower your heels to feel a deep stretch in the soleus.
Press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
Hold the squeeze, then return under control.
common_mistakes: Lifting the hips off the seat
breathing_pattern: Exhale while raising, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Sit in the machine with the pads against the inside of your knees/thighs. Adjust the machine to a wide, comfortable stretch.
execution_steps: Squeeze your thighs together, pushing against the pads until they meet in the middle.
Pause and squeeze the inner thighs.
Slowly let the pads return outward to the starting stretch position.
common_mistakes: Letting the weight stack crash at the bottom
Setting the stretch too wide and causing pain
breathing_pattern: Exhale while squeezing together, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Sit in the machine with the pads resting against the outside of your knees. Lean slightly forward or sit straight depending on target fiber preference.
execution_steps: Push your knees outward against the pads as far as possible.
Squeeze the side glutes hard.
Slowly return to the center under control.
common_mistakes: Using momentum to slam the pads open
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pushing out, inhale while returning.
progressions: Lean forward to target more gluteus maximus

exercise_setup: Set the Safety Squat Bar in a rack. Step under the yoke and hold the front handles. The camber of the bar pushes the weight forward, making it a hybrid between a front and back squat.
execution_steps: Keep your chest up and core braced.
Sit your hips back and down into a deep squat.
Drive through the whole foot to stand back up. The bar will actively try to fold you forward; fight to stay upright.
common_mistakes: Letting the bar push your chest toward the floor
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace before descending, exhale while standing up.

exercise_setup: Set the safety pins in a power rack at the bottom of your squat depth. Place the barbell on the pins and load it. Crawl under the bar into the bottom squat position.
execution_steps: Get tight, brace your core, and establish perfect form while wedged under the bar.
Drive explosively from a dead stop to stand up with the weight.
Carefully lower the bar back to the pins, let the weight settle completely, and repeat.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back trying to heave the weight up
Bouncing the bar off the pins
breathing_pattern: Inhale and brace hard at the bottom, exhale at lockout.

exercise_setup: Hold a barbell in the crooks of your elbows (Zercher hold). Clasp your hands together and keep your chest extremely tall.
execution_steps: Step backward or forward into a lunge position, lowering your back knee to hover just above the floor.
The weight will try to pull your torso forward; resist this by bracing the core intensely.
Drive through the front heel to stand back up.
common_mistakes: Letting the barbell slip down the forearms
breathing_pattern: Inhale while descending, exhale while standing.

exercise_setup: Lie on your back. Press a loaded barbell straight over your chest and hold it there (as if at the top of a floor press). Keep your legs straight and on the floor.
execution_steps: Lift your legs up and sweep them toward the left weight plate like a windshield wiper.
Lower them back to the center (without touching the floor), then sweep them toward the right plate.
Keep your arms locked and use your core to control the legs.
common_mistakes: Losing stability in the arms and dropping the barbell
breathing_pattern: Breathe steadily throughout the movement.

exercise_setup: Get into a wide push-up position with hands turned slightly outward.
execution_steps: Lower your body toward your right hand, bending the right elbow while keeping the left arm completely straight.
Your body should shift laterally.
Push through the right hand to return to the center, then lower toward the left hand.
common_mistakes: Not shifting the weight entirely to the working side
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering to one side, exhale while pressing to center.

exercise_setup: Get into a push-up position, but lean your body forward so your hands are near your waist/lower ribs, not your chest. Turn your hands outward or backward to protect your wrists.
execution_steps: Lower your body while maintaining this extreme forward lean.
Keep your elbows tucked tightly to your sides.
Press back up, pushing your shoulders forward and down.
common_mistakes: Losing the forward lean on the way up
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pressing.

exercise_setup: Hang from a pull-up bar or rings. Pull your knees tightly into your chest to form a tuck position.
execution_steps: Keeping your arms perfectly straight, engage your lats to pull your body backward until your back is parallel to the floor.
Hold this tucked position horizontally.
Resist the urge to bend your elbows or let your hips drop.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows (turning it into a row)
Not getting the back parallel to the floor
breathing_pattern: Breathe shallowly into the braced core.

exercise_setup: Place hands on parallettes or the floor. Squat down and tuck your knees into your chest.
execution_steps: Lean your weight forward onto your shoulders and hands.
Lift your feet off the ground, supporting your entire body weight on your hands while keeping your knees tucked tightly to your chest.
Keep your arms locked straight and protract your shoulder blades (round your upper back).
common_mistakes: Not leaning forward enough to lift the feet naturally
breathing_pattern: Take shallow breaths continuously into a tightly braced core to maintain stability.

exercise_setup: Hang from a pull-up bar. Lift your legs straight out in front of you until they are parallel to the floor, forming an L-shape with your body.
execution_steps: Maintain this strict L-sit position.
Perform a pull-up by pulling your chest to the bar.
Lower yourself under control without letting the legs drop.
common_mistakes: Dropping the legs during the pull
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Drape two thick towels over a pull-up bar, shoulder-width apart. Grip one towel tightly in each hand.
execution_steps: From a dead hang, pull your chest up to the level of your hands.
The towels will try to slip out of your hands; crush them with maximum grip force.
Lower under control back to a dead hang.
common_mistakes: Letting go of the towels and falling
Not fully extending the arms at the bottom
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Attach Fat Gripz to a barbell or dumbbells. Stand tall holding the weight with a supinated (underhand) grip. The thick grip prevents your hands from closing completely.
execution_steps: Keeping your elbows pinned to your sides, curl the weight upward.
Squeeze the biceps and forearms intensely.
Slowly lower the weight. The forearms will fatigue much faster than the biceps.
common_mistakes: Dropping the weight due to grip failure
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Set a low cable pulley. Stand facing away from the machine, holding the handle. Step forward slightly so your arm is pulled behind your torso, stretching the bicep.
execution_steps: Keep your elbow locked in position behind your body.
Curl the handle forward and up toward your shoulder.
Squeeze the peak, then slowly let the cable pull your arm back to the stretched position.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbow swing forward during the curl
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling, inhale while extending.

exercise_setup: Set an incline bench between two low cable pulleys. Grab a handle in each hand and sit back on the bench. Let your arms hang straight down and slightly back.
execution_steps: Keep your elbows pinned in place.
Curl both handles up toward your shoulders simultaneously.
Slowly lower back down. The cables provide constant tension at the bottom stretch, unlike dumbbells.
common_mistakes: Lifting the head/chest off the bench
breathing_pattern: Exhale while curling, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Set a cable pulley to waist/knee height. Hinge forward so your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Grab the cable (no attachment needed) and pin your upper arm to your side.
execution_steps: Keeping your upper arm completely still, extend your elbow backward until your arm is fully straight.
The cable provides tension at the peak contraction, unlike a dumbbell.
Slowly return to a 90-degree elbow bend.
cues: Pin the elbow to the ribs
breathing_pattern: Exhale while kicking back, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Stand facing the landmine. Hold the loaded end of the barbell with both hands, arms straight down in front of your hips.
execution_steps: Keep a slight bend in your knees.
Hinge at the hips, pushing your glutes backward and lowering the weight until you feel a deep stretch in the hamstrings.
The landmine arc naturally guides your hips back.
Drive your hips forward to stand up.
breathing_pattern: Inhale while hinging back, exhale while standing up.

exercise_setup: Stand sideways to the landmine. Hold the end of the barbell with your outside hand, resting it across the front of your body near the opposite hip.
execution_steps: Keeping a slight bend in the elbow, raise the barbell out to the side and slightly forward, following the natural arc of the machine.
Raise until your arm is parallel to the floor.
Slowly lower it back down.
breathing_pattern: Exhale while raising, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Stand in the Smith machine, holding the bar with a pronated grip slightly narrower than shoulder-width.
execution_steps: Pull the bar straight up along the front of your body toward your chin.
Keep your elbows pointing up and out, ensuring they stay higher than your wrists.
Lower the bar back to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Pulling the bar too high (above the collarbone) causing impingement
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Attach a rope to a low cable pulley. Stand facing the machine, holding an end of the rope in each hand.
execution_steps: Pull the rope straight up toward your upper chest, pulling your hands apart as you reach the top.
Keep your elbows higher than your wrists.
Slowly lower back down. The rope allows your wrists and shoulders to move more freely than a straight bar.
common_mistakes: Not pulling the hands apart at the top
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pulling up, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Place a thick pad on the floor under a Smith machine or barbell. Kneel on the pad and position the bar across your upper back.
execution_steps: Sit your hips back toward your heels as far as comfortable.
Drive your hips forward to push the bar up, returning to a tall kneeling position.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top.
common_mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back at the top
Not using a thick enough pad and hurting the knees
breathing_pattern: Inhale while sitting back, exhale while driving forward.

exercise_setup: Set a bench to a low/moderate incline on blocks so a barbell can slide under it. Lie face down with your chest supported. Grab the barbell with an overhand grip.
execution_steps: Pull the barbell straight up toward the underside of the bench by driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower the bar back to a full dead hang without letting it touch the floor.
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest off the bench
breathing_pattern: Exhale while rowing, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Set a bench to a high incline facing away from a low cable pulley. Grab the bar, sit on the bench, and let the cable pull your arms back over your head.
execution_steps: Keep your upper arms pointing toward the ceiling and stationary.
Extend your elbows to press the bar straight up.
Slowly lower the bar back behind your head, feeling a deep stretch in the triceps.
common_mistakes: Moving the upper arms (turning it into a press)
breathing_pattern: Exhale while extending, inhale while lowering.

exercise_setup: Attach a D-handle to a high pulley. Grab it with a supinated (underhand) grip. Stand facing the machine.
execution_steps: Pin your elbow to your side.
Push the handle straight down until your arm is fully extended.
Squeeze the triceps, then slowly return to the starting position without letting the elbow drift forward.
common_mistakes: Using body weight to push down
breathing_pattern: Exhale while pushing down, inhale while returning.

exercise_setup: Secure your legs on a decline bench and lie back, holding a dumbbell with both hands straight over your chest.
execution_steps: Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head.
The decline angle increases the stretch on the lats at the bottom of the movement compared to a flat bench.
Pull the dumbbell back over your chest.
common_mistakes: Going too heavy and straining the shoulders
Lifting the head off the bench
breathing_pattern: Inhale while lowering, exhale while pulling back.

exercise_setup: Attach a weight plate to a neck harness and put the harness on your head. Sit on a bench, leaning your torso forward so it rests on your thighs.
execution_steps: Let the weight pull your head down toward your chest, stretching the back of your neck.
Slowly extend your neck, lifting your head up and back to look straight ahead.
Hold the squeeze, then control the weight back down.
common_mistakes: Overextending the neck past a natural range
breathing_pattern: Exhale while extending up, inhale while lowering.
